title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High-Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure.
abstract: NA: Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities-such as metal-dielectric-metal nanopatch antennas-offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP-positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

title: Lewis Acid-Activated High-Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide for Superior Seawater Electrolysis.
abstract: NA: Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride-induced corrosion. In this study, we introduce Zn2+ as a Lewis acid site into high-entropy layered double hydroxide (LDH) to modulate both the interfacial microenvironment and the bulk electronic structure. The resulting catalyst requires overpotentials of 35 and 160 mV for the hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions at 10 mA  cm-2, respectively, accompanied by small Tafel slopes. Furthermore, an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer demonstrates operational stability over a duration of 900 h at 1.5 A  cm-2. Theoretical and in situ analyses reveal that Zn2+ exhibits a preference for adsorbing OH-, thereby repelling Cl-. Concurrently, this process induces oxygen vacancies and optimizes the d‑band centers of Fe/Co sites, establishing a interfacial/bulk dual regulation. This work offers a novel paradigm for the design of robust high‑entropy catalysts via Lewis acid doping for practical applications in harsh environments.

title: Bioinspired Buffered Microenvironment Enables Highly Crystalline 3D COF Gels With Controllable Structures for Exceptional Molecular Adsorption.
abstract: NA: Reconciling long-range crystallinity with macroscopic network formation remains a central challenge in constructing three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF) gels. Inspired by biomineralization and tofu coagulation, we propose a synergistic buffered system with salt bridges for direct assembly of crystalline 3D COF gels via imine condensation. Ten metal salts were selected to regulate stable and buffered pH microenvironment. Comparing various salts revealed a correlation between pH microenvironment and the formation state and crystallinity of COFs. NaAc emerges as representative regulator for multiple roles: (i) forming AcO-/AcOH buffer to maintain a stable weakly acidic microenvironment and promote disorder-to-order transition, (ii) regulating kinetics, defect healing, and COF topology, and (iii) Na+ as salt bridges stabilizing the 3D gel network. Pore topology can be switched between two crystalline phases by varying side substituents and salt addition sequence, as seen by XRD peak shift from 8.9° to 6.6°. The gels have low density (0.028-0.042 g/cm3), high compressive strength, CO2/N2 selectivity of 140, organic solvent uptake up to 80 times their weight, and over 90% capacity retention after 20 cycles. Overall, this work establishes a paradigm from microenvironment engineering and ion selection to topology regulation and adsorption, providing a blueprint for functional 3D COF gels.

title: Synergistic Dual-Site Regulation in a Tailored Imine-COF for Enhanced Hydrogen Peroxide Photosynthesis.
abstract: NA: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) emerge as promising candidates for the photocatalytic production of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2). However, precise modulation of the chemical environment of active sites in COFs remains a significant challenge. Based on a molecular engineering strategy, this study focuses on hierarchical regulation of nitrogen coordination environments for efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production through the 2e- ORR. Intrinsic nitrogen configurations (triazine vs. pyridine) are first tailored to construct two types of COFs. The pyridyl-imine TAPT-BTPA (4) optimizes charge carrier separation and extends visible-light absorption, leading to an enhanced H2O2 production rate of 8.12 mmol g-1 h-1 in aqueous solution containing isopropanol as a sacrificial agent under an O2 atmosphere. Main-group metals (In, Sn, and Sb) are then anchored at the pyridine-imine sites to modulate local electron density further and steer reaction pathways. Structural characterization and activity tests reveal that Sb-coordinated TAPT-BTPA-Sb (10) induces a unique synergistic effect, redirecting the ORR toward a more favorable stepwise 1e- route. This significant pathway regulation ultimately boosts the H2O2 production rate to 15.3 mmol g-1 h-1 under the same conditions. This work clarifies the decisive role of coordination environment engineering and establishes a molecular-level design paradigm for advanced H2O2 synthesis photocatalysts.

title: Bridge-Level Electronic Compensation in Prussian White Cathodes: Charge-Transfer Kinetic Regimes and Design Principles.
abstract: NA: Prussian White (PW) cathodes are promising sodium-ion battery materials because of their open framework, low cost, and high structural reversibility. However, polarization and capacity loss under high-rate or low-temperature operation arise from coupled ionic, structural, interfacial, and electronic processes that are not fully captured by Na+ diffusion or average structural evolution alone. This perspective introduces a bridge-level electronic-compensation framework in which the Fe─C≡N─TM bridge is treated as a local unit for describing local charge redistribution. Using Marcus-type descriptors together with concepts of metal-to-metal charge transfer, intervalence charge transfer, and metal-ligand interactions, three physical contributions are emphasized: the local charge-state free-energy difference (ΔG°), cyanide-mediated electronic coupling (Hab), and structure-coupled reorganization energy (λ). Local bridge states are organized into descriptor-based kinetic regimes based on the balance among energetic mismatch, electronic coupling, and structural reorganization, with transition-metal chemistries serving as representative mechanistic cases. These descriptors are further translated into design principles involving redox-level alignment, cyanide-mediated coupling and network connectivity, and control of local structural reorganization. This perspective provides a physical basis for interpreting bridge-level electronic compensation and considering how local energetic alignment, coupling, and structural reorganization can be regulated in PW cathodes.

title: Intranasal Pathogenesis-Adaptive Nanotherapeutics Reinstate Regenerative Competence for Post-Stroke Neural Repair.
abstract: NA: Poststroke neurorehabilitation is limited by the poor regenerative capacity of adult neurons. Although neural stem cells (NSCs) can generate new neurons, their reparative potential is constrained by inefficient delivery to cerebral lesions and a hostile regenerative niche. Here, analysis of a single-nucleus transcriptomic dataset revealed pronounced dysfunction and intercellular crosstalk among neurons, microglia, and NSCs, highlighting redox imbalance and impaired nitric oxide (NO) signaling as potential therapeutic targets. Guided by these findings, we develop FCeO2@GLp, a pathogenesis-adaptive nanotherapeutic integrating reactive oxygen species scavenging, NO replenishment and immune modulation within cerebral ischemic microenvironment. Following intranasal administration, FCeO2@GLp actively adheres to the olfactory epithelium (OE), reaches infarcted brain regions, releases cerium oxide (CeO2) nanozyme, fingolimod, and a NO donor in response to local acidity. This coordinated strategy alleviates oxidative stress, reprograms microglia, protects neurons, and enhances NSC proliferation and neuronal differentiation. Consequently, FCeO2@GLp effectively reduces infarct volume and cerebral edema during the acute phase, and improves long-term neurological function and survival, establishing a lesion-responsive strategy for poststroke neural repair.

title: Deciphering Roles of Interfacial Tunable Primer for High Active Material Contents Pure Silicon Electrodes.
abstract: NA: While pure silicon (Si) is a highly attractive anode material for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries, its practical implementation is limited by severe volumetric fluctuations during cycling. This intrinsic instability inevitably induces continuous structural degradation, strictly restricting the maximum allowable active material fraction within the electrode. To address this critical challenge, we design an interfacial tunable functional primer (fp) that serves as an effective multi-component bridging agent. By optimizing the mechanical resilience and electrochemical cohesion among electrode components, the fp layer dissipates interfacial stress and secures continuous electron conduction pathways. Furthermore, the unique ionophoric properties of the benzoxazine framework directly regulate the interfacial solvation structure and enhance ion flux. Driven by these integrated effects, the fp-modified Si anode achieves remarkable electrochemical reversibility even at a nearly binder-free composition containing 99 wt% active material content. This strategy completely averts the rapid physical degradation typically observed in standard binder networks under such extreme formulations. Furthermore, fp-modified Si demonstrates practical viability by assembling double-stacked pouch cells paired with NCM90 cathodes, which exhibit long-term cycle durability. This study provides a highly effective paradigm for electrode-component regulation and molecular-level engineering in pure Si anode interfacial modification strategies.

title: A Janus Bilayer Portland Cement-Based Moisture-Electricity Generator via Hydrogen-Bonding Network Regulation.
abstract: NA: The ubiquitous interaction between ambient moisture and built environments presents a compelling opportunity for continuous energy harvesting through moisture-electricity generation (MEG). However, current MEG materials fail to satisfy high-power demands in buildings because hydrogen bonds, indispensable for the structural integrity of soft carbon-chain networks, severely restrict water diffusion, and thus bottleneck MEG performance. Hydrated Portland cement, featuring a robust silicate backbone, allows aggressive modulation of the water hydrogen-bonding network (HBN), emerging as an ideal platform for higher performance. Here, we developed a Portland cement-based moisture-electricity generator (CMEG) via a facile asymmetric acid etching strategy, extending MEG to cementitious material systems. The resulting CMEG presents a Janus bilayer architecture with a stark gradient in hygroscopicity across the layers to drive the unidirectional diffusion of water molecules. Mechanistically, the etching process induces the breakage of HBN, which unlocks ultrafast water diffusion throughout the top layer and thus accelerates selective ion transport toward the bottom layer. Remarkably, CMEG delivers an extremely high short-circuit current density of 723 µA/cm2 and output power density of 112.5 µW/cm2. Furthermore, CMEG demonstrates exceptional scalability, modular integration capabilities and nearly identical mechanical strength to that before acid etching, proving its giant potential for future self-powered buildings and infrastructures.

title: Staged Network Evolution Enables In Situ Strengthening and On-Demand Recyclability of Polyurethanes via Dynamic Sulfilimine-Urea Bonds.
abstract: NA: Cross-linked polymers exhibit exceptional mechanical robustness, dimensional stability, and chemical resistance arising from permanent covalent networks. However, it remains challenging to tune mechanical properties after curing and to decouple on-demand recyclability from in-use stability. Herein, we report a staged network evolution strategy based on dynamic sulfilimine-urea bonds to address these demands. The rapid room-temperature addition of isocyanates to sulfilimines forms dynamic sulfilimine-urea linkages, affording a solvent-resistant initial polyurethane (SUP-S1). Subsequent thermal treatment of SUP-S1 induces dissociation of the sulfilimine-urea linkages, regenerating the sulfilimine motifs and releasing isocyanates that are captured in situ by backbone hydroxyl groups to form thermodynamically stable urethane bonds. The tensile strength and toughness of the obtained polyurethane (SUP-S2) are significantly enhanced, increasing from 17 to 42 MPa and from 55 to 158 MJ m-3, respectively, while the Young's modulus is retained. Moreover, the photoclip of sulfilimine motifs facilitates on-demand recyclability by reducing the cross-link density. The resulting recyclable polyurethane (SUP-S3) exhibits excellent multi-recyclability, retaining over 96% of its mechanical properties after five recycling cycles. This staged network evolution design reconciles the enhancement of mechanical properties with end-of-life recyclability within a single material platform, providing a robust pathway for the development of next-generation sustainable cross-linked polymeric materials.

title: A Coaxial Bioprinted Hydrogel With Semipermeable Sheath and Pro-Chondrogenic Core for Articular Cartilage Repair.
abstract: NA: Stem cell-laden hydrogels represent a promising strategy for the functional repair of articular cartilage defects. However, the pathological joint microenvironment is often characterized by persistently elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, which severely compromise transplanted cell survival and impair their chondrogenic differentiation potential. Inspired by the hierarchical mechanical gradient of native cartilage, we developed a sheath-core biomimetic hydrogel (SCGAE) via embedded coaxial bioprinting, featuring a robust poly(ethylene glycol)-alginate (PA) sheath that spatially integrates mechanical support and immunoprotection around a soft, bioactive gelatin methacryloyl-alginate-decellularized extracellular matrix (GAE) core. The dense PA sheath provides immediate mechanical support and functions as a size-selective diffusion barrier, permitting nutrient and oxygen permeation while effectively blocking inflammatory cytokines (>40 kDa). This protective niche enables the pericellular matrix-mimicking GAE core to maintain stem cell viability >89% under pro-inflammatory conditions and support robust chondrogenic differentiation. In a rabbit osteochondral defect model, bone marrow stromal cell-laden SCGAE constructs promoted substantial cartilage repair, achieving defect filling, host integration, and regeneration of glycosaminoglycan-rich hyaline-like cartilage. This sheath-core architecture design spatially integrates structural, mechanical, and immunoprotection functions, presenting a promising platform for the regeneration of load-bearing articular cartilage.

title: Constructing Low-Friction Ion Transport Pathways in Crosslinked Polymer Electrolyte for Practical Quasi-Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: Quasi-solid-state polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with high energy density, but still suffer from sacrificed ionic conductivity caused by electrolyte solidification. Here, by tuning monomer structures with different Li+-affinity, we investigate the decisive role of the segmental solvation ability of the polymer matrix in cation transport. Owing to the overly strong affinity for cations, conventional ether segments significantly decrease the Li+ relaxation rate, and the resulting "sticky" polymer chains impede Li+ migration. In contrast, the weakly coordinating segments such as fluorinated ether could effectively minimize coupling with Li+ ions, thereby constructing "low-friction" cation transport pathways in crosslinked polymer electrolytes, as reflected by the nearly unchanged Li+ relaxation kinetics and high ionic conductivity. Therefore, the industrial Li metal pouch cells achieve excellent comprehensive electrochemical performance under harsh lean-electrolyte conditions, with electrolyte dosage even as low as 1.3 g Ah-1. The 2 Ah NCM811/Li cell exhibits an extended lifespan beyond 520 cycles and maintains stable operation across a wide temperature range from -50°C to +90°C. The 8.7 Ah NCM955/Li cell delivers 550 Wh kg-1 energy density and demonstrates impressive cycling stability over 260 cycles. This work could inspire fundamental understanding and further development toward practical LMBs.

title: Scalable Hydrogel-Programmed Porous Photonic Cement for Passive Daytime Cooling.
abstract: NA: Cement is among the most widely produced materials on Earth, yet its strong solar absorption causes building envelopes to act as heat sources, increasing cooling energy demand. Here, we structurally program cement hydration to transform conventional cementitious materials into passive cooling interfaces. Through hydrogel-confined mineralization of cement clinker, we construct a robust, hierarchically porous calcium-silicate-hydrate (C-S-H) network that integrates broadband light scattering, vapor transport and thermal insulation. By regulating the composition and crystallinity of the hydrates, the material achieves ∼95% solar reflectance and ∼98% infrared emissivity without the use of additional photonic fillers. The hygroscopic nature of the network further enables sustained evaporative cooling under humid or cloudy conditions where radiative cooling alone becomes inefficient. Life-cycle analysis indicates that this strategy provides a pathway to transform high-emission cement into carbon-mitigating materials integrated within opaque building envelopes, enabling the scalable deployment of daytime radiative cooling across the built environment.

title: In Situ Topological Dealloying Enables Atomically Coupled Metal-Oxide Heterostructures.
abstract: NA: Metal-oxide heterostructures are central to energy conversion and electronic devices because interfaces can modulate the configuration coupling among charge, spin, and orbit. However, conventional synthesis routes suffer from structural incompatibility and weak coupling, which hinder the universal construction of atomically coupled metal-oxide heterointerfaces. Here, we develop an in situ topological dealloying strategy to construct metal-oxide heterostructures with atomically interconnected interfaces. This strategy can be broadly applied to perovskite, spinel, columbite, and vanadate oxides, which enables the spontaneous formation of high-density magnetic nanoalloys embedded within dielectric oxide matrices. Direct nanoscale visualizations of electric and magnetic fields reveal the coexistence of interfacial charge polarization and vortex-like spin textures. These emergent dielectric and magnetic behaviors arise from atomically interfacial hybridization that mediates strong charge-spin interactions. When integrated into flexible architectures, these heterostructures exhibit broadband GHz-frequency absorption (effective absorption bandwidth up to 6.6 GHz at 3.0 mm), high efficiency, and rapid electromagnetic-to-thermal energy conversion under microwave irradiation. This work establishes a general route to engineer metal-oxide heterostructures for functional applications.

title: An Engineered Thio-Amino Polymer Achieves Potent, Safe, and Broad Cell Type Delivery in the Lung Mapped by Spatial Transcriptomics.
abstract: NA: Efficient delivery of nucleic acids to the lung has the potential to impact future respiratory treatments. Current formulations exhibit significant limitations, including insufficient potency, single-cell delivery characterizations, efficacy demonstrations in disease models, and toxicology assessments. Here we describe polymer 81 (P81), which, when used with hypotonic solvents, is 34.1- to 77.8-fold more potent than previous polymers with various cargos for lung transfection by nebulized mRNA. Through the exploration of multiple routes of administration, P81 demonstrated a wide of range of cell-type delivery, including bronchial airway epithelial cells, tracheal basal stem cells, and 54% of all cells in the distal lung, assessed via single-cell spatial transcriptomics. Robust expression of mRNA-encoded antibodies in the lung by P81 enabled quantification of target protein and successful suppression of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The toxicology assessments of multiple doses of P81 polyplexes via nebulization in rodents were unremarkable. Overall, P81 represents a step forward for inhaled nucleic acid delivery to the respiratory tract, positioning itself as an efficient, safe, and translatable delivery formulation.

title: Polymer-Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template-Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single-Crystalline Mn2OBO3.
abstract: NA: Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer-directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template-free synthesis of mesoporous single-crystalline Mn2OBO3 (MSC Mn2OBO3). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn2+ ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single-crystalline MnBO2OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn2OBO3. As an anode active material for lithium-ion batteries, MSC Mn2OBO3 delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g-1 at 0.2 A g-1, more than twice that of bulk Mn2OBO3. Notably, this polymer-directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn2OBO3 (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single-crystalline materials for energy storage.

title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π-Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro-Crosslinking-Network for Flexible Polymer Light-Emitting Diodes.
abstract: NA: Stretchable fully π-conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic-deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft-micro-crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable p-n FπCPs (PX-OXI1-X-HDI) films with a recoverable-deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three-dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro-crosslinked network formed by oxime-urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro-crosslinked p-n FπCPs free-standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on PX-OXI1-X-HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm-2. Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro-crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m-2, revealed the excellent cycle-deformation-stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro-crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long-term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Determining Composition-Structure-Property Relationships in Quaternary Perovskitoids Through Megalibraries.
abstract: NA: Understanding how composition governs structure and function is essential for designing functional materials, however, establishing these relationships remains prohibitively slow for materials with massive and tunable compositional spaces, such as Bi and Sb-based perovskitoids. Here, a novel megalibrary-based synthetic methodology has been developed and used to rapidly identify and characterize quaternary perovskite derivatives across an expansive compositional space. Parylene templates were used to synthesize one million compositionally distinct, positionally encoded Cs3Sb2-xBixBr9-yIy microcrystals on 2 × 2 cm2 chips with 20 µm periodicity. These megalibraries enabled the systematic investigation of structural and optoelectronic evolution across this compositional space using micro-area x-ray diffraction, position-resolved absorbance spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and confocal fluorescence microscopy. An unusual non-monotonic bandgap shift was observed with increasing Br content, reaching a minimum at 33% Br. This behavior is attributed to the formation of halide-segregated heterostructures, consisting of low-dimensional, I-rich shells surrounding Br-rich layered cores. Phase separation was most pronounced in Sb-rich compositions, which were found to stabilize heterostructure formation. This study demonstrates how megalibraries enable the simultaneous evaluation of key optoelectronic parameters, including bandgap and phase purity, revealing complex, composition-dependent structure-function relationships in perovskitoids and providing a versatile platform for accelerating the discovery of optoelectronic-relevant materials.

title: Skunk Cabbage-Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence.
abstract: NA: Near-infrared (NIR)-responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade-offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra-fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR-responsive actuators by integrating aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus-structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra-low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi-donor-π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor-acceptor interactions and molecular motion-facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat-transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.

title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial- and Mesenchymal-Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC-Derived Intestinal Organoids.
abstract: NA: Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill-defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG- and Matrigel-cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation-associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM-remodelling and integrin-associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2-positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

title: Pd Single-Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self-Decoupled Temperature-Humidity Dual-Mode Sensors.
abstract: NA: The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high-fidelity multi-modal temperature-humidity sensing without inter-channel cross-talk and computational post-processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron-ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self-decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single-atom anchoring and heterogeneous-nucleation-driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus-response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra-fast quasi-2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy-driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross-talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low-temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi-modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed-loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on-demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next-generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ-Formed Ceramic-Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation.
abstract: NA: Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water-rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross-linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual-mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm- 3) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame-inhibiting SO2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic-carbon hybrid barrier. Post-test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO4) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically "weld" B2O3 to carbon. This trend in BO4 fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high-performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi-stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next-generation battery safety materials.

title: pH-Responsive Synthetic Cells for Programmable In Situ Protein Synthesis and Release.
abstract: NA: Lipid membrane-bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell-like compartments for on-demand biomolecule production. However, most cell-free gene expression systems in synthetic cells are regulated by user-imposed cues rather than signals associated with environmental or physiological states. Here, we present an acidity-transducing synthetic cell that converts external pH changes into nucleic acid information to drive in situ protein synthesis. The system integrates gramicidin A proton channels for pH sensing, triplex-forming single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that releases a trigger ssDNA upon acidification, and a toehold switch RNA that activates translation in response to the released trigger ssDNA. This work further reveals that tuning the annealing length between the pH-responsive and trigger ssDNAs controls the trigger-release pH, which is critical for enabling acid-triggered protein synthesis. The synthetic cells retain their pH-responsive activity when embedded in alginate hydrogels, creating acidity-responsive materials that synthesize proteins in situ rather than release preloaded cargo. Cell-penetrating peptide tagging further enables selective protein release and target-specific binding. This work establishes a molecular transduction strategy for programming synthetic cell materials to sense environmentally relevant acidity and generates functional biomolecules on demand.

title: Preserving Polymorphic Crystalline Structures in Bulk Heterojunctions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non-fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non-halogenated mixed-solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS2) and o-xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high-performance acceptor BTP-eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat-film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide-angle x-ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing-incidence wide-angle x-ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single-crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non-radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II-based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm2 active area) fabricated by slot-die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution-processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single-crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.

title: A Dual-Locked and H2S-NO Tandem-Activatable NIR-II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics.
abstract: NA: Dual-locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual-locked systems only restricted to enzyme-responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker-responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near-infrared (NIR-II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual-locked and gas tandem-activatable NIR-II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water-dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid-responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN-NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible-NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN-NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H2S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR-II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN-NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type-I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR-II fluorescence imaging-guided efficient photo-elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual-locked and H2S-NO tandem-activatable nanoagents with gas-responsive and NIR-II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

title: Sensitive, Broadband, and Stable Short-Wave Infrared Photodetection and Imaging in Mixed-Dimensional Organic/Inorganic Heterostructures.
abstract: NA: Conventional short-wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed-dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier-collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices' performance. Herein, a type-II band-aligned PTF/WSe2 mixed-dimensional heterostructure is reported for high-performance broadband SWIR photodetection via heterostructure synergy and rational Schottky barrier engineering. The Cr/p-WSe2/PTF configuration (∼ 0.28 eV barrier) achieves superior performance, while Cr/n-WSe2/PTF suffers from a higher barrier (∼ 1.18 eV). The optimized device achieves broad spectral photoresponsivity (∼ 103 A/W, 1060-1470 nm) and exceptional performance at 1310 nm: ultrahigh photoresponsivity (R = 2894 A/W), robust specific detectivity (D* = 1.0×1012 Jones), and excellent long-term ambient stability. Versus standalone PTF, it delivers 17-fold higher photoresponsivity and 96% lower bias voltage. High-resolution SWIR image-pattern reconstruction, together with concurrent performance improvements after six months of controlled storage, validates this PTF/WSe2 mixed-dimensional heterostructure's potential for advancing next-generation high-performance SWIR detectors.

title: Ultralow Loading Iridium Doped Hollandite Manganese Oxide Nanowires for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction.
abstract: NA: Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow-loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, <16 µgIr cm- 2) integrated within a hollandite MnO2 framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm- 2 from 580 mV (undoped α-MnO2) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrOx. Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP-MS dissolution measurements with x-ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH- and potential-dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir-efficient mixed-metal oxide catalysts.

title: Sustainable Soft Electronic Devices by High-Performance Recyclable Elastomers and Conductors.
abstract: NA: Soft electronics have driven emerging advancements, which are expected to have wide-range and large-scale applications in health management, electronic skins, soft robotics, and interactive human-machine interfaces. However, existing strategies mainly focus on isolated components, and system-level soft electronic devices combining sustainable fabrication, robust performance, and versatile integrated functions have rarely been explored. Herein, we develop a recyclable soft electronic system enabled with multifunctional poly thioctic acid (TA) elastomer and high-performance elastic metallic conductors. The multifunctional TA elastomer exhibits an exceptional combination of stretchability (435% strain), fracture energy (5.5 kJ/m2), apparent adhesion energy on Cu (10.7 kJ/m2), and thermal conductivity (0.69 W/m·K). These properties enable robust mechanical and electronic interfacing with different electronic components for sustainable soft circuits, while also endowing the electronic systems with outstanding self-healing and recycling capabilities. Furthermore, by integrating with printable and recyclable elastic conductors based on eutectic liquid metals, the sustainable soft electronic systems can fully restore circuit functionality after complete mechanical rupture with the selfhealing capability of the composite elastomer and the elastic conductor. The system can be reprocessed to achieve full functionality restoration. The materials strategy developed in this study renders a promising solution for the development of soft and sustainable electronic devices.

title: Fluoride-Mediated Host-Activator Engineering in Homogeneous Lithium Glass Scintillators for Thermal-Neutron Detection and Imaging.
abstract: NA: Homogeneous lithium-aluminosilicate-glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride-mediated host-activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce3+-activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F- preferentially coordinates with Li+ and Mg2+, preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter-tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host-network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect-mediated trapping, modulates medium-range Ce-centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce-concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO2 (twice that of GS20). After 6Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron-1, an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak-to-trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6Li-enriched glass scintillator, achieving single-digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3He proportional counters and high-performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof-of-concept two-dimensional thermal-neutron imaging with a system-level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position-sensitive neutron imaging.

title: Upcycling Piezoelectric Single-Crystal Debris Into High-Performance Flexible 0-3 Composites.
abstract: NA: High-value piezoelectric single-crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor-based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off-cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling-to-device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-PbTiO3 (PMN-PT) single-crystal debris into high-performance flexible 0-3 piezoelectric composites and energy harvesters through material-structure-mechanics co-design. A ball-milling-based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)-assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi-1-3-like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single-crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a d33 of 118.5 pC N-1 while retaining mechanical flexibility, placing it among the highest-performing flexible 0-3 piezoelectric composites. Comparative experiments and finite-element simulations reveal that single-crystal-derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP-induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm- 2. This work establishes a scalable upcycling pathway for reutilizing high-value functional crystal waste in flexible self-powered electromechanical systems.

title: Rate Capability of Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Oxide Cathodes: Charge-Discharge Kinetics, Multiscale Bottlenecks, and Dynamic Rate-Determining Steps.
abstract: NA: Lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g-1 through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next-generation high-energy-density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast-charging applications. This review deconstructs rate-limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge-transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate-determining step (RDS) shifts from electron-transfer to ion-diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density (j0) and the limiting current density (jd). Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often-overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high-rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross-study C-rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high-rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.

title: Correction to "Colorful Electrochromic Displays With High Visual Quality Based on Porous Metamaterials".
Ion-Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision.
abstract: NA: A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single-channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion-electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual-channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic-light-guided closed-loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This "single device enabled, distinguishable dual-channel readouts" principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10H-Pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium Salts.
abstract: NA: Next-generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent-free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation-caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion-π+ interactions. Specifically, a rigid N-doped fluorene (10H-pyrido[1,2-a]-5-indolium, PIn+) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent-free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

title: Dynamic, Wet-Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair.
abstract: NA: Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self-repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial-based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet-adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid-covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff-base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine-containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self-healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane-derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host-graft integration, and cartilage-like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet-adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial-cartilage interface healing in fluid-rich joint environments.

title: High-Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging.
abstract: NA: Metasurface-enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high-throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade-off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction-enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high-quality-factor resonances. By embedding bound-state-in-the-continuum metapixels within a bandgap-engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three-dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal-to-noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single-shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral-spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one-to-one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single-pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real-time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.

title: Discovery of Small-Molecule Cryoprotectants Using Pretrained Language Model Representations.
abstract: NA: Cryopreservation supports cell therapy, transfusion medicine, and tissue banking, but cryoprotectant selection remains constrained by empirical screening, toxicity, and ice recrystallization. We used pretrained language models as SMILES sequence encoders to prioritize small-molecule cryoprotectants for experimental testing. Hierarchical representations were coupled to descriptor reconstruction, gated fusion, and downstream prediction of normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels. Splat-cooling measurements assessed candidate ice recrystallization inhibition, followed by compatibility and cryopreservation experiments in red blood cells, human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells and rat abdominal aortas. Selected additives improved recovery or preservation endpoints within the tested formulations. This representation-based screening workflow connects molecular property prediction with experimental cryobiology across ice, cellular, and tissue endpoints.

title: Bismuth-Mediated Zinc Extraction-Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single-Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction.
abstract: NA: Fe single-atom catalysts with Fe-N4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi-mediated Fe-adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe-N4 moieties on ZIF-8-derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe-N-pCd catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half-wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi-solid-state Zn-air battery using Fe-N-pCd as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at -40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe-N4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH-bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect-modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d-band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe-*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential-limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring-template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

title: Quantum Saturation of the Electro-Optic Effect.
abstract: NA: Future quantum computing architectures require electro-optic materials that maintain a strong, stable performance at cryogenic temperatures. In conventional electro-optic materials, large electro-optic coefficients are often confined to narrow temperature windows near structural phase transitions, where small changes in temperature lead to large changes in the electro-optic response. Using thermodynamic analysis, phase-field simulations, experimental growth, and cryogenic optical measurements, we show that quantum fluctuations can be harnessed to overcome this trade-off. By tuning the ferroelectric phase boundaries down to 0 K, quantum fluctuations induce a saturation regime in which a large electro-optic response becomes nearly temperature-independent below 25 K. We demonstrate that the phase boundaries can be tuned through either strain in BaTiO3 or through chemical composition in Ba1- xCaxTiO3, leading to a large, temperature-insensitive, cryogenic electro-optic response, reff =  2850 pm V-1 (experiment) and r51 =  2900 pm V-1 (theory) for BaTiO3 on GdScO3 and r51 =  1898 pm V-1 (theory) for Ba0.77Ca0.23TiO3. These values exceed the room temperature performance of bulk BaTiO3 r51 =  1600 pm V-1 and surpass the cryogenic performance of BaTiO3-on-Si, reff =  200 pm V-1, by over an order of magnitude. These findings establish a general design principle for engineering high-performance electro-optic materials for cryogenic applications.

title: Engineering High-Performance Flexible Electronics Through Scalable Manufacturing: Interplay of Materials, Processing, and Morphology.
abstract: NA: Flexible electronics have garnered extensive attention in recent years considering their promising applications across diverse fields such as communications, energy, display, healthcare, and wearable devices. Unlike laboratory-scale fabrication and integration, the transition of flexible electronics toward commercial applications demands scalable manufacturing that ensures high performance, large-area reproducibility, high yield, and throughput. However, achieving scalable manufacturing while maintaining device performance remains challenging, as fabrication scale-up often induces variations in material assembly, morphology evolution, and device integration, which may compromise functional reliability achieved at the laboratory scale. Generally, current flexible electronic devices can be divided into two categories: planar-type and fiber-type devices, representing two complementary platforms for realizing large-scale and highly integrated systems. In this review, scalable fabrication strategies tailored for each category and the latest advances are systematically summarized. In particular, the interplay among material design, scalable processing, morphology evolution, and device integration is highlighted, with emphasis on strategies that preserve device performance during manufacturing scale-up. Representative planar-type and fiber-type flexible electronic systems are further discussed to demonstrate how the synergistic optimization of material design and scalable manufacturing approaches enables high-performance devices for diverse applications. Finally, we outline remaining challenges and future directions to inform future developments in scalable flexible electronics.

title: Coupling Iodine Conversion and Zinc Ion Transport via Molecular Catalysis for Long-Life Zinc-Iodine Batteries.
abstract: NA: Zinc-iodine (Zn-I2) batteries are attractive for low-cost and scalable energy storage owing to their rapid iodine redox and high theoretical capacity. However, their practical application is severely limited by polyiodide shuttling and interfacial mass-transport imbalance, where polyiodide immobilization and Zn2+ accessibility are difficult to reconcile for continuous redox compensation, especially under high-rate conditions. Here, we address this adsorption-transport conflict by screening a series of metalated tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin molecular catalysts and identifying iron (III) meso-tetrakis (4-carboxyphenyl) porphyrin (Fe-TCPP) as a unified interfacial regulator catalyst. The Fe-N4 center provides moderate polyiodide binding, thereby stabilizing iodide intermediates without inducing interfacial passivation. Meanwhile, peripheral carboxyphenyl groups create a zincophilic microenvironment that promotes Zn2+ accessibility and local ion compensation. This coordinated regulation synchronizes electron transfer and ion redistribution, thereby sustaining reversible iodine redox while avoiding transport blockage. As a result, the Fe-TCPP-regulated iodine cathode delivers a specific capacity of 178 mAh g-1 and sustains 50 000 cycles at 5 A g-1. Moreover, a pouch cell with a high iodine loading of 22 mg cm-2 operates stably for more than 1300 cycles. This work establishes a molecular-catalytic framework for the simultaneous regulation of redox-intermediate adsorption-conversion and ionic transport in aqueous batteries involving soluble redox species.

title: Atomic-Scale Design, Performance Degradation Mechanisms, and System Integration of Multi-Principal Element Hydrogen Storage Materials.
abstract: NA: Solid-state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room-temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid-state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic-scale design to system-level performance. A unified composition-process-structure-property framework is established that integrates engineering-driven design rules, post-processing techniques, multi-scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high-throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic-scale origins and cross-scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen-induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel-cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA-based solid-state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de-/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.

title: Spin-Selective Hydrogen Utilization Enables Efficient Electrochemical CO2-to-CH4 Conversion in Ag-Modified Chiral Cu Catalysts for Unassisted Solar Fuel Production.
abstract: NA: Although electrochemical CO2-to-CH4 conversion offers a viable pathway to sustainable fuel synthesis, its efficiency is limited by the difficulty of balancing the availability of reactive hydrogen species for multistep CO2 hydrogenation against the suppression of the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we establish a spin-selective catalytic strategy using Ag-modified chiral Cu electrocatalysts to overcome this intrinsic trade-off. Structural chirality in the Cu framework induces chirality-induced spin selectivity, which disfavors spin-singlet H2 formation, thereby mitigating the HER and favoring productive hydrogen utilization toward CO2 hydrogenation. Ag modification facilitates the supply of *CO intermediates on adjacent Cu sites. Thus, the chiral Ag/Cu catalyst selectively drives CO2 reduction toward CH4, delivering a CH4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 67.0% at -0.7 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode while suppressing the HER. When coupled with perovskite-based photoelectrochemical electrodes, the chiral catalyst enables unassisted solar-driven CO2-to-CH4 conversion with an FECH4 of 54.1% and a solar-to-fuel efficiency of 5.86%. These results suggest spin-selective hydrogen utilization as an effective approach to selective hydrocarbon synthesis and bias-free solar CO2-to-fuel conversion.

title: Breaking the Capacity-Reversibility Linear Trade-Off in Li-O2 Batteries via Amorphous Non-Precious High-Entropy Alloy Catalysts.
abstract: NA: Lithium-oxygen (Li-O2) batteries suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and rely on precious metal-based catalysts to facilitate the reaction process. Despite being effective, these costly catalysts would inevitably introduce a critical trade-off between capacity and reversibility, compromising the high energy density advantage of Li-O2 batteries. In this study, we have designed an amorphous non-precious MnFeCoNiCu high-entropy alloy (A-HEA) catalyst via a mild liquid-phase reduction strategy to break the above inherent linear trade-off. The amorphous and porous structure of A-HEA could provide a large electrochemical active surface area, diluting the local current density to promote the solution-mediated discharge pathway. This enables the growth of large-sized Li2O2 to deliver a discharge capacity reaching 10.8 mAh cm-2. Additionally, the multielemental synergistic electron redistribution of A-HEA optimizes the d-band center to strengthen the LiO2 adsorption and weaken the O─O bonding, reducing the overpotential to 0.75 V and extending the battery lifetime by 4-5 times compared to the crystalline counterparts. Importantly, the A-HEA can be produced at a scale of over 100 g and works well in Li-O2 pouch cells with a rate capability up to 400 mA and an energy density of 754 Wh kg-1 (560 Wh kg-1 even at -30°C).

title: Ferroionic-Assisted, Charge-Driven Polymorphic Phase Engineering for Multilevel Memristive Devices.
abstract: NA: Memristive device operation can arise from diverse microscopic mechanisms, including charge polarization and trapping, magnetic ordering, ionic migration, and structural phase transitions. Among these, crystalline-crystalline phase transitions in polymorphic materials offer a unique platform for nonvolatile resistance modulation but are often hindered by large energy barriers and limited endurance. Here, we demonstrate a multimodal, charge-driven phase modulation in an atomically thin polymorphic material, Mo0.92W0.08Te2, enabled by electrostatic coupling to a ferroionic substrate, CuInP2S6. The polymorphic channel exhibits reversible switching between semiconducting and metallic phases via electrostatically accumulated charges, reflecting the intrinsically low energy barrier between its competing polymorphs. Integration with the ferroionic substrate enables spatially localized, nonvolatile charge accumulation in the channel, which provides distinct, programmable phase-control pathways under a two-terminal bias configuration. The phase-induced resistance modulation through field-driven ionic processes is governed by the evolution of a phase-dependent Schottky junction at the electrode-channel interface, yielding multiple, stable conductance states under pulsed electrical excitation. Leveraging these experimentally derived synaptic characteristics, we conducted an MNIST inference simulation with a convolutional neural network, achieving 98.45% accuracy. This ferroionic-assisted phase-engineering strategy offers new opportunities beyond traditional phase-change devices for adaptive electronic and neuromorphic material platforms.

title: Design of Heteroatomic Active Sites for Electrochemical COx Reduction Toward Multicarbon Products.
abstract: NA: The electrochemical CO2 and CO reduction (COxRR) to value-added multicarbon (C2+) products offers a promising route for sustainable carbon recycling and renewable fuel generation. Although Cu catalysts exhibit unique activity, these single-metal sites are constrained by linear scaling relations of intermediate adsorption energies, which limits further improvements in selectivity and energy efficiency. Introducing heteroatoms to regulate active-site coordination provides an effective approach to transcend these limitations. This review describes recent advances in the theoretical design, controllable fabrication, and mechanistic investigation of heteroatomic active sites for COxRR toward C2+ products. Theoretical identification for high-performance sites through descriptor-based modeling, data-driven screening, and dynamic simulations is first discussed. Then, the precision synthesis strategies for constructing atomically dispersed, long-range-ordered, and interfacial-confined heteroatomic structures are systematically summarized. Subsequently, mechanistic insights into the promoting effect of heteroatoms, driven by synergistic electronic and geometric modulation, are highlighted, followed by an analysis of future research directions and the key challenges for the industrial implementation of heteroatomic catalysts for COxRR. This review provides an integrated perspective linking active-site design to catalytic performance, offering guidance for the development of next-generation heteroatomic electrocatalysts for efficient COxRR toward the sustainable production of high-value chemicals.

title: Surface-Coordinated Gas-Solid Polymerization Enables Quasi-2D Polyphenylacetylene Single-Crystalline Nanoribbons.
abstract: NA: Two-dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer single crystals are highly desirable for optoelectronics, yet their realization is limited by the intrinsic coupling between molecular-weight buildup and chain entanglement, which disrupts long-range order. Here, we report a gas-solid interfacial polymerization strategy that decouples monomer diffusion from chain propagation, enabling the growth of quasi-2D polyphenylacetylene (PPA) single-crystalline nanoribbons on Cu/CuOx surfaces. This process is likely enabled by surface coordination-assisted activation of phenylacetylene and directional π-stacking-driven assembly, which suppress chain entanglement and promote crystallographic ordering. As a result, micrometer-scale PPA single-crystalline nanoribbons with left-handed cis-transoidal helical chains and long-range crystallinity are obtained. Under an ideal fully extended-chain model, the PPA chains exhibit a geometrically estimated upper-bound molecular weight of up to ∼3.7 × 109 g mol- 1. The resulting PPA nanoribbons exhibit efficient charge transport and broadband photodetection from 375 to 1550 nm, with a responsivity of 30.1 A W- 1 and a detectivity of 8.65 × 101 2 Jones. This interfacial synthesis strategy provides a route to overcoming the trade-off between molecular-weight buildup and structural order in conjugated polymers, offering opportunities for quasi-2D polymer semiconductors in flexible optoelectronics and programmable chiral materials.

title: Twistsonics: Engineering Acoustic Topological Textures in Moiré Sound Lattices.
abstract: NA: Moiré superlattices formed by twisting periodic systems provide a powerful platform for emergent topological phenomena, but their use for programming real-space topology in acoustic wave fields remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a phase-controlled spoof surface acoustic wave platform for constructing moiré topological textures in the acoustic particle-velocity field. On a perforated acoustic metasurface, two twisted skyrmion lattices are synthesized and superposed, yielding acoustic skyrmion bags with controllable topological numbers and geometries. The twist angle and rotation center control the scale and configuration of the bags, enabling deterministic reshaping of the composite texture. We further introduce controlled defects to assess the defect tolerance of the moiré skyrmion bags. The skyrmion bags retain their composite topology over a finite range of defect fractions, and comparison with an untwisted single-layer skyrmion lattice suggests enhanced stability of the enclosed skyrmion cluster relative to the single-layer reference at higher defect fractions. The same programmable platform also supports transitions from skyrmion lattices to meron lattices and enables twist-induced meron clusters. These findings establish acoustic moiré superlattices as a reconfigurable platform for engineering robust real-space topological textures, with potential applications in topology-guided acoustic manipulation and information encoding.

title: Rigid Double-Spiro-Grid Polymer Regulates Donor Fibrillar Pre-Assembly and Acceptor Interdiffusion in Layer-by-Layer Organic Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Layer-by-layer (LBL) fabrication of organic solar cells (OSCs) decouples donor and acceptor deposition, which, however, induces difficulties in controlling donor crystallization and acceptor interdiffusion. Here, we introduce NPSG, a fully conjugated double-spiro-grid polymer, to regulate donor fibrillar pre-assembly before acceptor deposition. Morphological results reveal that NPSG shifts D18 assembly from loosely associated aggregates toward pronounced fibrillar pre-assemblies in solution. Molecular dynamics simulations further suggest that the rigid NPSG backbone provides multiple noncovalent interaction sites that favor anisotropic association between D18 chain segments. During film formation, these fibrillar precursors evolve into a coherent and solvent-resistant donor framework, which moderates L8-BO interdiffusion and promotes a vertically graded, double fibrillar heterojunction. The resulting morphology facilitates interfacial charge transfer, improves the balance of electron and hole transport, and suppresses nongeminate recombination. Consequently, the optimized D18+NPSG/L8-BO devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.2%, with a certified value of 20.7%. This strategy also improves device reproducibility, processing tolerance, applicability across different donor/acceptor systems, and operational stability under maximum-power-point (MPP) tracking. These findings establish donor-underlayer pre-assembly regulation as an effective strategy for efficient and robust sequentially processed OSCs.

title: Tailored Cationic Visible-Light-Active Interfaces for Sustainable, Biodegradable Nanofibers With Dual-Mode Antimicrobial Activity and Robust Electrostatic Particle Capture.
abstract: NA: The accumulation of microplastics originating from single-use personal protective equipment presents a growing environmental concern. Developing biodegradable fibrous alternatives is essential, but integrating robust antimicrobial efficacy with stable electrostatic capture while maintaining degradability remains a critical challenge. Here, we report a surface co-functionalization strategy addressing these challenges through covalent immobilization of sodium copper chlorophyllin (SCC) and quaternary ammonium compounds (QAC). Beyond simple dual functionalization, this molecular design induces intramolecular charge separation, suppressing electron-hole recombination in SCC and thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species generation under visible light. Simultaneously, QAC introduce permanent cationic surface charges that enable contact-mediated microbial inactivation and humidity-resistant electrostatic particle capture. Demonstrated on biodegradable silk nanofibers as a model substrate, the functionalized fibers exhibit potent antibacterial and antiviral activity under both dark and illuminated conditions, together with high nanoparticle capture efficiency. Importantly, the fibers retain intrinsic biodegradability, undergoing near-complete degradation under enzymatic conditions and substantial decomposition in soil environments. This work establishes a versatile surface functionalization platform applicable to diverse fibrous substrates, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional microplastic-generating protective materials.

title: Interface-Confined Cationic Polarization Enables Rapid and Reversible Polyiodide Conversion for High-Rate Zinc-Iodine Batteries.
abstract: NA: Aqueous zinc-iodine (Zn-I2) batteries are promising for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their application is limited by sluggish polyiodide redox kinetics and severe shuttle effect. Many cathode-regulation strategies improve iodine chemistry through physical confinement and polar adsorption. However, simultaneously suppressing polyiodide shuttling and enabling rapid iodine conversion remains challenging, particularly under high-rate where fast interfacial redox kinetics are required. Here, interface-confined cationic polarization is established by integrating π-delocalized guanidinium cations (Gdm+) into iodine cathodes, where cation-π interactions with Ketjen Black (KB) sp2 carbon domains confine Gdm+ on the KB surface. The delocalized positive charge of interface-confined Gdm+ electrostatically enriches polyiodides within the cathode, while its delocalized π-electron system polarizes the electron cloud of iodine species and promotes interfacial charge transfer, enabling reversible polyiodide conversion without irreversible trapping. The optimized I2 cathode delivers 100 mAh g-1 at an ultrahigh-rate of 50 A g-1 (∼237 C) and sustains 40 000 cycles with only 0.002% decay per cycle. A 1.0 Ah pouch cell retains 82.6% capacity after 1200 cycles. This work demonstrates interface-confined cationic polarization as an effective strategy for regulating polyiodide redox chemistry, offering a new route toward high-rate and long-life Zn-I2 batteries.

title: Heterostructure Design in Two-Dimensional Perovskites by Sequential Recrystallization.
abstract: NA: Low-dimensional metal halide perovskites provide exciting opportunities to fabricate new semiconductor materials. Semiconductor technology relies on electronic heterojunctions, and cost-efficient and flexible approaches to realize functional heterostructures are of fundamental importance. Lateral heterostructures define the energy landscape in the plane of the semiconducting lattice in 2D perovskite materials, representing an ideal platform to tailor energy barriers and to control charge carrier flow.
