However, the long-term stability of metal-nitrogen-carbon atomic-site catalysts (M-N-Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the "buckets effect" of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi-N-C dual-atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ2-O electron modulator for long-life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O-coordinated vicinal Fe-Ni configuration. The µ2-O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N-site protonation and intermediate-induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H2O2/ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination-engineering strategy for designing durable M-N-C catalysts for long-life RZABs.

title: In Situ Constructed Pore-Chain Interlocked Networks in Polyimide-Covalent Organic Framework Nanocomposites Enable Ultralow k Dielectrics for High-Fidelity Signal Transmission.
abstract: NA: The ultralow k porous polymer dielectrics have been widely explored for Integrated circuit (IC) interconnects, 5G/6G communications, and wearable devices. However, disordered pore structures and poor interfacial adhesion remain a major challenge, thus making it difficult to decouple the k-tanδ trade-off. Here, we employ hollow covalent organic frameworks (H-TD-COF) as multifunctional molecular anchoring nodes to construct robust pore-chain interlocked networks in polyimide nanofibrous films. The amino-functionalized COF shells participate in the in situ growth of polyimide (PI) chains, thus enabling interlocked interfaces that fundamentally restrict segmental mobility and suppress dipolar relaxation. Subsequent electrospinning technique allows anchored chains to be stretched along the fiber axis and immobilizes them within an oriented fibrous architecture. This simultaneously disrupts long-range charge migration pathways while preserving stress-transfer and heat-dissipation continuity. The resulting PI-g-COF(4) nanocomposites with 4 wt% H-TD-COF loading achieve an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50 and dielectric loss of 0.001 at 1 kHz, with highly stable dielectric properties up to 250°C. Notably, device-level measurements further reveal a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SINAD) of 22.30 dB under 200 MHz crosstalk interference, showing a 52.2% improvement over commercial polyimide. This work lays solid foundations for nanoscale interfacial regulation in porous polymer nanocomposites towards ultralow k dielectrics.

title: Optically Tunable Chiral Magnetic States and Exchange Engineering via Charge-Transfer Excitation in a van der Waals Antiferromagnet CrPS4.
abstract: NA: Controlling magnetism with light in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets could enable ultrafast, energy-efficient spintronics. However, selectively writing distinct magnetic phases, such as chiral magnetic states (e.g., spin spirals and skyrmions) for memory and collinear states for logic, within a single material remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic, photon-energy-selective writing of magnetic order in the air-stable antiferromagnet chromium thiophosphate ( CrPS4 ). Its ligand-to-metal charge transfer gap serves as an intrinsic switching threshold: excitation below this gap drives d - d transitions to stabilize chiral magnetic states due to a spin-spiral phase, while excitation above activates a photo-doping mechanism that renormalizes magnetic exchange and induces a collinear phase. These optically defined states are distinguished through polarization-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy and probed via a proximal monolayer tungsten diselenide ( WSe2 ). By establishing optical selectivity in a single material, our work provides a reconfigurable platform for opto-spintronic circuits where memory and logic functions can be dynamically toggled with light.

title: Sub-nm2 Ferroelectric Domains via Charged 180° Walls in ZrO2.
abstract: NA: Flat phonon bands in fluorite ferroelectrics ( HfO2 or ZrO2 ) shrink polar domains laterally to an irreducible half-unit-cell width ( ∼ 0.27 nm) within which the vertical arrangement of dipoles is expected to remain uniform. Here, we report on the direct observation of nonuniform and nearly discrete vertical arrangements of dipoles in ZrO2 thin films consisting of closely spaced head-to-head (HH) and tail-to-tail (TT) charged 180 ∘ walls, each exhibiting a distinct bulk-like structure. These charged domain walls (CDWs) further compress the irreducibly narrow, laterally stacked domains vertically to a thickness of ∼ 1-2.75 nm, yielding in-plane domains with sub- nm2 footprints-among the smallest ever reported for any ferroelectric material. The HH and TT walls form due to their flat longitudinal optical (LO) polar bands, and the former are electrostatically stabilized by bound-charge compensation via interstitial oxygen atoms, which act as natural structural defects at the HH walls. Moreover, these walls are predicted to be conducting and to exhibit ultralow propagation barriers, with HH walls (1.6 meV) being far more mobile than TT walls (22.3 meV), indicating strong potential for low-voltage, domain-wall-based nanoelectronics.

title: Industry-Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET-Cu Current Collectors.
abstract: NA: Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film-typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high-temperature operation. Here, we report an industry-scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al2O3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll-to-roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min-1, substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al2O3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte-induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long-term cycling. The as-resulting Al2O3-coated PET-Cu CC (PET@Al2O3-Cu CC) enables 3-Ah graphite//LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C-comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET-Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low-cost and industry-scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost-efficient and high-energy LIBs.

title: High-Entropy Materials as a Design Paradigm for Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Batteries.
abstract: NA: Low-temperature (LT) operation remains a major barrier to the practical deployment of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) because reduced thermal activation magnifies coupled limitations in bulk Na+ transport, phase stability, and interfacial kinetics, resulting in strong polarization growth, rapid capacity loss, and poor rate capability. Conventional optimization approaches based on incremental compositional tuning target a single bottleneck at a time and therefore struggle under sub-zero conditions, where transport and interphase evolution become tightly intertwined. High-entropy materials (HEMs) offer a distinct design paradigm in which configurational disorder is used as a controllable variable to reshape thermodynamics and kinetics, stabilize vulnerable frameworks, and broaden the distribution of accessible Na+ migration pathways. In this review, we analyze how entropy engineering influences LT performance across cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, and interfaces, emphasizing mechanistic links between realized disorder, transport activation penalties, and the accumulation of interfacial resistance in the solid-electrolyte interphase and cathode-electrolyte interphase. We synthesize quantitative descriptors and minimum reporting metrics that enable meaningful comparison across studies, and we highlight a unifying entropy-percolation framework connecting bulk ionic conduction with solvation/desolvation and interphase transport in liquid systems. We conclude by outlining key trade-offs, manufacturability constraints, and research directions required to translate high-entropy strategies into robust LT-SIB operation.

title: Magneto-Propelled Micromotors for Integrated Capture and Catalytic Upcycling of Micro/Nanoplastics.
abstract: NA: The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical-Mn/N-doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time-resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near-complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic "hot spots" at the Au-micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N-doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO4 •‒-mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate-determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale-up conditions, with a machine learning model (R2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno-economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value-added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.

title: Biodegradable Capacitive-Coupling Bioelectronics for Wireless Electrical Stimulation and Longitudinal Electrophysiological Monitoring of Peripheral Nerve Regeneration.
abstract: NA: Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive-coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo-wire interconnects, and a textile-reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio-NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery-free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB-mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro-regenerative immune modulation, calcium-related signaling, AMPK-associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB-enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic-monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.

title: Strain-Insensitive Conductors for Stretchable Electronics.
abstract: NA: Stretchable electronics are rapidly evolving from simple planar configurations to complex, three-dimensional (3D) multifunctional architectures. However, traditional stretchable conductors frequently suffer from severe resistance fluctuations under mechanical deformation. To address this challenge, this review systematically summarizes two core design paradigms for achieving robust strain insensitivity. The first paradigm, corresponding to structurally strain-insensitive conductors, relies on a top-down geometric decoupling strategy that physically dissipates strain through 3D buckling or kirigami structures. The second paradigm, corresponding to intrinsically strain-insensitive conductors, employs a bottom-up network reconstruction strategy that leverages the fluidic adaptability of liquid metals or the dynamic sliding of nanofillers to sustain continuous percolation networks under stress. Beyond these fundamental paradigms, we comprehensively evaluate precise fabrication processes and critical system-level integration challenges, with a particular focus on in-plane modulus mismatch and Z-axis interlayer shear failure. Importantly, this review highlights the indispensable role of strain-insensitive conductors in advanced applications, demonstrating their unique capability to eliminate motion artifacts in bioelectronics, lock resonant frequencies in wireless communications, and ensure thermal safety in high-power actuation platforms. Finally, we outline future trajectories for large-scale industrial manufacturing and long-term in vivo stability, aiming to accelerate the commercialization of technologies within this interdisciplinary field.

title: Advanced Nanomedicines for Cancer Metabolic Therapy.
abstract: NA: Abnormal metabolic reprogramming is a recognized hallmark of cancer, yet the clinical translation of cancer metabolic therapy (CMT) by conventional chemo-drugs remains a great challenge due to their poor drug targetability, short circulation time, and low bioavailability. Nanomedicines, owing to their great feasibility in rational designs, facile fabrication, and excellent biocompatibility, offer a powerful platform to overcome the drawbacks of current clinical drugs and enable precise modulation of cancer metabolism. In this review, we provide a critical overview of recent advances in nanomedicine-based CMT. We first summarize the reprogrammed metabolic landscape of cancer cells and the metabolic crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment. Then, nanomedicine strategies targeting glucose, lipid, amino acid, nucleotide, and carboxylic acid metabolism are summarized and discussed in a comprehensive way, with an emphasis on nanomaterial design principles and regulatory mechanisms. Finally, key challenges and future prospects for clinical translation are discussed, aiming to establish nanomedicine-enabled CMT as a next-generation paradigm for effective and safe cancer treatment.

title: Biomass DNA: An Emerging Building Block for Advanced Materials.
abstract: NA: Since the structural discovery of DNA's double helix, it transitioned from a genetic carrier to a cornerstone of programmable nanotechnology and materials science. However, while synthetic DNA with predesigned sequences has dominated DNA-based materials, biomass DNA, naturally derived from bulk biological resources, has emerged as a powerful large-scale engineering material. This review outlines biomass DNA-derived materials and their multifunctional applications, framed as a "Biomass DNA Tree," representing biomass resources as roots, duplexes as stems, and advanced materials as leaves. For example, we examine the transformation of biomass DNA into sophisticated 3D-crosslinked hydrogel matrices for (bio)engineering, and their further processing into recyclable bioplastics, which supports carbon neutrality. Furthermore, we highlight biomass DNA organogels and fibers, as well as its utilization for energy storage, including supercapacitors, batteries, and interphase layers. Beyond these core areas, the review highlights breakthroughs applying DNA as functional materials for catalysis, soft robotics, OLEDs, medical patches, neuromorphic devices, and photoconductors. By addressing challenges and providing perspectives on future opportunities, this review aims to catalyze the next generation of materials science, emphasizing the role of biomass DNA in advancing biopolymer-based applications.

title: Interface-Mediated Architectural Engineering of Silicon for Solid-State Batteries: Current Status and Future Outlook.
abstract: NA: Solid-state lithium batteries promise superior performance and enhanced safety over current lithium-ion batteries. As lithium metal encounters intrinsic challenges, high-capacity silicon anodes have gained increasing attention to satisfy the growing demand for higher energy density and safety. However, the commercialization of such systems is impeded by challenges including large volume variation, poor interfacial contact, sluggish charge transport, inferior performance, and excessive pressure reliance. This review discusses fundamental challenges and interface-mediated architectural engineering strategies. Based on the coupling mode of silicon and solid electrolyte, the developed architectures are classified into three representative categories, with emphasis on their design principles, multiscale construction methodologies, and enhancement mechanisms. In light of the latest advances, this review systematizes the architectural paradigms, and clarifies the synergistic correlations between interfacial compatibility, electron and ion transport, stress relaxation, and side reactions between silicon and solid electrolyte. Scalable manufacturing protocols and sustainable monitoring approaches are then delineated toward practical applications. Finally, the review summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of these classifications and outlines future directions for advancing stable, safe, scalable, and sustainable silicon-based electrode technologies for viable solid-state batteries with enhanced energy density, power capability, durability, and manufacturability at low-pressure operation.

title: Spontaneous Capture, Enrichment, and SERS Sensing of Polystyrene Micro/Nanoplastics Enabled by Condensed Plasmonic Coacervate Droplets.
abstract: NA: Pervasive contamination by micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) poses threats to environmental and human health; however, their sensitive detection is challenged by low concentrations and lack of effective enrichment methods. Herein, we present a plasmonic coacervate platform that spontaneously sequesters polystyrene (PS) MNPs from water while facilitating surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection. Coacervate microdroplets, formed through the liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of cationic poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) and anionic adenosine triphosphate, exhibit a positive surface charge and a hydrophobic interior, enabling capture of nanoscale or microscale negatively charged PS MNPs with enrichment rates of 99.4% and 91.1%. The co-encapsulation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) generates three-dimensional droplet-confined SERS hotspot networks, resulting in an enhancement factor of 2.72 × 109, excellent uniformity, and minimum detectable concentration of 1 and 10 ng/mL for nano- and micro-scale PS, demonstrating strong linear correlations. This platform achieves recoveries ranging from 87% to 108% for PS MNPs spiked into filtered tap and river water and successfully detects PS MNPs released from commercial plastic cups and expanded polystyrene containers under simulated daily use. Our work establishes a simple, rapid, and sensitive strategy that integrates spontaneous analyte sequestration with plasmonic amplification, thus offering a new avenue for monitoring MNPs and assessing the safety of food-contact materials.

title: Mechanoactive Biomaterials for Cell-Matrix Mechanotransduction.
abstract: NA: Cells and extracellular matrices (ECMs) form mechanically coupled feedback loops in which cells generate forces, remodel their surroundings, and respond to mechanical information returned by the matrix. Conventional biomaterial models have established how passive matrix properties, including stiffness, viscoelasticity, architecture, and ligand presentation, regulate this feedback, but they provide limited control over the dynamic mechanical inputs transmitted through living tissues. Mechanoactive biomaterials address this limitation by converting external or encoded triggers into mechanical inputs with defined timing, magnitude, frequency, and spatial localization. Here, we compare mechanochemical hydrogels, light-responsive matrices, thermoresponsive systems, and optothermal mechanoactuators according to the material response, the mechanical input experienced by cells, spatial, and temporal control, reversibility, cytocompatibility, quantification, and translational constraints. We discuss how these platforms engage integrin-focal adhesion signaling, mechanosensitive ion channels, cytoskeletal and nuclear mechanotransduction, YAP/TAZ activity, and TGF-β activation. We conclude with design principles for selecting reversible or persistent actuation, matching mechanical parameters to receptor and tissue mechanics, and advancing mechanoactive platforms toward predictive in vitro models.

title: Atomic-Level Regulating Layer-by-Layer Zinc Deposition by High-Entropy Single-Atoms Electrolyte Additive.
abstract: NA: Aqueous batteries feature intrinsic safety, but how to achieve regular and planar electrodeposits at liquid-solid interfaces has emerged as a fundamental barrier to energy-dense aqueous batteries that use metal anodes. Based on classical crystal growth theory, sluggish metal ion transport during the deposition process will lead to rapid interfacial metal ion depletion, resulting in a sharp increase in interfacial supersaturation and subsequently inducing dendrite growth. Herein, micropore high-entropy single-atoms carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) were synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to suppress interfacial Zn2+ concentration polarization and strengthen Zn chemistry at the atomic level. The micropore CuNiMnCoIr/CNs not only provide abundant Zn2+ transport channels but significantly reduce the migration energy barrier of Zn2+ from the bulk electrolyte to electrode interface to promote rapid desolvation kinetics and homogenize Zn2+ flux, thereby effectively alleviating interfacial Zn2+ supersaturation and guiding layer-by-layer Zn deposition. Consequently, trace CuNiMnCoIr/CNs additive delivers a high Zn2+ transference number of 0.89 and enables Zn//Zn cells to cycle stably for over 4000 h at 5 mA cm-2, and 800 h even at 50 mA cm-2, with an outstanding cumulative deposition capacity up to 20 Ah cm-2. Such knowledge may provide new insights to challenge interface chemistry for advanced aqueous metal-ion batteries.

title: Nanoarchitectonics With Static-Dynamic Synergistic Interfacial Remediation for Practical Zinc Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: Aqueous zinc metal batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage because of their high safety and low cost, yet their practical deployment remains limited by dendrite growth, parasitic reactions, and the gradual failure of interfacial protection during prolonged cycling. Here, we report a static-dynamic synergistic interfacial remediation strategy in which a preconstructed In/Sb interfacial layer is coupled with a dynamically responsive electrolyte additive to mitigate continuous interfacial degradation. Specifically, a dual-phase In/Sb composite layer (ISZ) is formed on Zn by spontaneous galvanic replacement, providing a compact and chemically stable interface that promotes uniform Zn deposition and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, In3+ in the electrolyte dynamically participates in anode-side regulation during cycling, assisting defect-responsive interfacial regeneration. Owing to this synergy, the ISZ-In3+ system delivers both improved initial deposition behavior and sustained interfacial stability during repeated plating/stripping. Symmetric cells operate stably for nearly 6000 h at low areal capacity, for about 500 h under 40 mA cm-2/20 mAh cm-2, and for over 1000 h at an ultrahigh Zn utilization rate of 95%. This strategy is further extended to Br2/Zn batteries, where pouch cells stably operate for nearly 3600 h and 700 h at areal capacities of 12.5 and 25 mAh cm-2, respectively. In addition, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling over 3600 h, and a low-N/P pouch cell (N/P = 1.46) cycles for nearly 1400 h, while a 400 mAh pouch cell achieves a component-level energy density of about 80 Wh kg-1, excluding the electrolyte and pouch packaging. This work provides a practical interfacial design strategy for high-capacity, long-life aqueous Zn batteries.

title: Supramolecular Adhesives with Tunable Crystallinity for Extreme Environments.
abstract: NA: Developing high-performance adhesives capable of withstanding harsh environments-specifically ultralow temperatures, water, acid, base and organic solvents-via low-cost, scalable manufacturing remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the architecture of spider silk, we report a facile strategy to fabricate a solvent-free supramolecular adhesive composed of tannic acid (TA) and poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL). Integrated theoretical and experimental investigations uncover the critical role of crystallinity modulation in governing adhesion performance. The resulting adhesive achieves an exceptional strength of up to 8.5 MPa at ambient temperature (25°C) and 6.6 MPa at cryogenic temperature (-196°C), outperforming existing commercial hot-melt adhesives. Furthermore, it exhibits remarkable stability in corrosive underwater environments (acidic, alkaline, and saline) and organic solvents. This work not only establishes a novel bioinspired design paradigm for adhesives operating under extreme conditions but also paves the way for the scalable production and practical applications of supramolecular materials.

title: Bridging Biosensing and Hardware-Level Data Security With a Conjugated Radical Polymer.
abstract: NA: The integration of biological signal processing with hardware-level data security remains a fundamental challenge in bioelectronic systems, where sensing and data protection are typically implemented as separate functional layers. Here, we present a conjugated radical polymer platform that exhibits stochastic electronic behavior and bioelectronic signal transduction within a single material system. The system displays stochastic resistive switching associated with its complex electronic structure and structural disorder, which enables physical unclonable function characteristics with uniqueness and uniformity approaching the ideal value of 50%. In parallel, the same material exhibits electrochemical signal transduction in an organic electrochemical transistor configuration, allowing highly sensitive dopamine detection with a detection limit of ∼10 pM, and a preferential response over the tested interferents. Systematic analysis indicates that the sensing response is consistent with redox-mediated coupling between dopamine and the radical-containing backbone. By establishing a material-level strategy that links stochastic electronic functionality and bioelectronic sensing, this work provides a pathway toward secure, adaptive, and biointegrated electronic systems.

title: Functional Group Transposition Enables Antiparallel-Parallel Packing Switching in Dithieno[3,2-b:2',3'-d]pyrrole Self-Assembled Molecules for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics.
abstract: NA: Concurrently regulating interfacial and bulk charge dynamics, which requires simultaneous control over indium-tin-oxide (ITO) interfacial properties and active layer morphology, is critical for advancing and integrating organic solar cells (OSCs) and photodetectors (OPDs). However, designing universal hole-transport-layers (HTLs) compatible with diverse photovoltaic platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose two regioisomeric acceptor-donor-acceptor type self-assembled molecules (SAMs) with dithienopyrrole (DTP) core. Simply swapping ortho-/para- positions of trifluoromethyl and chlorine on the phenyl termini switches molecular stacking from disordered antiparallel to well-ordered parallel. This programmable assembly benefits to yield uniform HTLs on ITO with homogeneous surface potential, alongside enhanced crystallinity and vertical phase segregation in the PM6:Y6 active layer. Optimized OSCs and OPDs achieve 18.70% power conversion efficiency (PCE) and a shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 6.52 × 1014 Jones at 805 nm (specific detectivity: 4.26 × 1013 Jones). The versatility of the optimized SAM is validated across state-of-the-art binary/ternary systems (PCE of 20.92% for D18:L8-BO:BTP-eC9 system), even upon scaling up (PCE of 19.1% for PM6:L8-BO:BTP-eC9 system, device area = 0.6 cm2). This work not only elevates DTP as a competitive alternative against carbazole for SAMs, but also establishes functional group transposition as a finely tuned molecular lever that co-engineers interfacial order and active-layer morphology toward high-performance organic optoelectronics.

title: Pollen-Engraved Dual Porosity Ceramic Beads From Liquid Marbles for Environmental Remediation.
abstract: NA: Liquid marbles, renowned for their non-wetting behavior, have been extensively investigated in the fields of controlled delivery, droplet reactors, and biomaterial storage. However, the transition in wetting interactions between the liquid droplet and the coating particles has not been clearly studied, and leveraging this transformation for new applications remains unexplored. Here, we use UV irradiation along with mechanical vibration to switch the wetting state at the liquid marble interface from Cassie-Baxter to Cassie-impregnating during a one-step process that converts liquid marbles into ceramic green bodies. Renewable biowaste pollen is, for the first time, employed to impart both surface patterning and internal porosity together with a photocured polymer, yielding dual-porosity ceramic adsorbents that achieve up to 2.88 times higher pollutant removal efficiency, particularly for heavy metal ions and nanoplastics. Furthermore, different pollen species exhibit distinct pollutant selectivity, underscoring their potential for environmental remediation.

title: Minimally Invasive In Vivo Fabrication of Multiscale Biohybrid Systems.
abstract: NA: Multiscale biohybrid systems integrating living materials with minimally invasive in vivo fabrication offer new opportunities for precise diagnosis, physiological monitoring, and tissue regeneration. This review provides a unified perspective on their design and therapeutic integration, organizing recent advances across multiscale material design, minimally invasive fabrication, spatiotemporal co-engineering, and functional applications. Three emerging principles are identified: multiscale coupling bridges material architectures with cellular and tissue responses; spatiotemporal coordination integrates precise in vivo construction with dynamic material and biological evolution; and sensing-regeneration feedback extends biohybrid systems from passive repair toward responsive therapeutic regulation. Building on these principles, we highlight machine learning-assisted material discovery, multi-site fabrication, and intelligent feedback control as key directions for developing adaptive, closed-loop therapeutic systems. Together, these insights provide design guidance for translating minimally invasive multiscale biohybrid systems toward next-generation patient-centered healthcare.

title: Programmable Structural Color Lifetimes via Activation Energy Engineering for Spatiotemporally Encoded Dynamic Optical Encryption.
abstract: NA: Spatiotemporally programmable structural color holds great promise for high-security optical encryption, yet precisely tailoring the lifetime of structural color across a broad temporal range spanning multiple orders of magnitude remains a significant challenge in polymer systems. The lifetime of structural color is intrinsically governed by the segmental relaxation kinetics of the underlying polymer network, which has been largely overlooked in the rational design. Here, we report a dynamic surface grating with programmable structural color lifetime, in which the optical evolution process is precisely encoded by tuning the activation energy through crosslinking density and amplitude control. Driven by segmental relaxation, the grating amplitude gradually decays over time, redistributing diffracted energy back to specular reflection and causing a gradual fading of structural color. By spatially encoding the relaxation activation energy via photomask-assisted UV exposure, the structural color lifetime governed by local amplitude decay kinetics can be independently programmed across different regions, spanning an unprecedented temporal range from 300 s to over 240 days. This strategy enables diverse applications, ranging from stimulus-responsive optical encryption and time-resolved multilevel information encryption to practical cold-chain integrity monitoring, establishing activation energy as a broadly applicable handle for temporal programmability in dynamic optical systems.

title: Supercapacitors Under Nonequilibrium Conditions: Mechanisms and Design Principles.
abstract: NA: Supercapacitors have attracted considerable interest as high-power energy storage devices for grid frequency regulation, backup power systems, and fast-response applications, which are increasingly operated under conditions far from equilibrium, including floating states, high-frequency cycling, rapid charge and discharge, wide temperature windows, and high-voltage regimes. Under these nonequilibrium conditions, performance and stability are governed by coupled kinetic and thermodynamic processes, including ion transport limitations, interfacial polarization, electrolyte decomposition, and structural stress evolution. These processes span multiple length and time scales, from ion desolvation and surface reactions through pore-level transport mismatch to macroscopic degradation. This review presents a unified perspective on the mechanisms that govern supercapacitor behavior under nonequilibrium conditions. Representative operating scenarios are analyzed to identify three common degradation origins, namely, transport mismatch, interfacial instability and thermo-mechanical coupling. Building on this mechanistic understanding, rational material-design principles are derived on ion transport regulation, interfacial chemistry regulation, electrolyte optimization, and structural adaptability. Finally, future research directions are discussed for bridging the gap between laboratory evaluation and real-world operation and for guiding the development of robust supercapacitors for dynamic energy storage applications.

title: Vitamin C-Induced Photo-Redox Threshold Enables High-Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen.
abstract: NA: Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter-scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell-matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible-light-activated Ru(II)bpy3 2+/sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near-immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo-redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high-fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post-printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post-printing and cell-laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell-instructive 3D microenvironments.

title: Decoupled Biomass Electrooxidation Over E-Waste-Derived Au Enables Low-Voltage H2 and Scalable FDCA Production.
abstract: NA: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low-potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value-added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion-template-assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH)2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride-coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low-voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow-electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm-2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low-potential aldehyde oxidation from high-potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low-voltage hydrogen production with high-value biomass conversion.

title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long-Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n-decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10-DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high-LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.

title: Closed Pores as Internal Stress-Regulation Units for Practical Silicon-Carbon Anodes.
abstract: NA: Silicon-carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high-energy lithium-ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation-induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress-regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon-carbon anodes. Heteroatom-doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion-induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li+ insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen-doped silicon-carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g- 1, an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g-1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine-learning-guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed-pore design. This work establishes closed-pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low-expansion silicon-carbon anodes.

title: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling.
abstract: NA: Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero-energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross-linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro-/nano-porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long-wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice-sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.

title: Robust Sodium-Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte-Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization.
abstract: NA: Sodium-metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next-generation energy-storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high-concentration, localized high-concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na+ transport and generating mechanically robust, ion-conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in-situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine-learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium-metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead-sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high-performance, practical sodium-metal batteries.

title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic.
abstract: NA: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium-ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value-added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two-dimensional material nanosheets (In2P3S9 NSs/Fe-Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high-value chemicals. The best-performing photocatalyst (Fe1.0Cu0.5) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g-1. Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy-kelvin probe force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In2P3S9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high-value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value-added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.

title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide-Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase-Like Activity for Liver Protection.
abstract: NA: Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)-mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active-site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide-hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic-organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure-activity analysis showed that GPX-like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide-hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide-hybrid analogue, and conventional metal-based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione-dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide-hybrid material protected against acetaminophen-induced and rifampicin-induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide-hybrid frameworks as effective GPX-like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress-associated liver diseases.

title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation-Type Framework Anodes for Fast-Charging Sodium-Ion Batteries.
abstract: NA: Intercalation-type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast-charging sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation-type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic-scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M-Na4Ti5O12/C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g-1 at 10 A g-1) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g-1) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na+ diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low-barrier, nanoscale ion-conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg-1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high-rate battery materials.

title: Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics.
abstract: NA: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell-type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route-specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell-resolved biodistribution, long-term safety, repeated-dose immunogenicity, cross-study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high-throughput screening, machine learning, and data-driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next-generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue- and cell-selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.

title: Chiral Phonon-Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non-Magnetic Ferroelectric.
abstract: NA: The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non-magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non-magnetic ferroelectric In2Se3 generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon-induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non-equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin-Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin-current generation. Polarization-resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization-dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non-magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4 Se8.
abstract: NA: Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three-dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination-resolved micro-ARPES, fine photon-energy mapping, spin-ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three-dimensional fermiology of the layered g-wave altermagnet CoNb4Se8 , obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H- NbSe2 . We resolve the spin-split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin-ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time-reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry-protected nodal Γ -K direction. We further report a weak low-temperature anomaly near T0 ≈ 50-60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature-dependent micro-ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum-resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross-Linked Polymer Enables Long-Calendar-Life Lithium Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross-linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross-linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in-situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion-derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg-1) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid-State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries.
abstract: NA: The discovery of new solid-state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile-ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile-ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion-migration barriers spanning Li-, Na-, K-, and Mg-ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆d, a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile-ion-neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short-range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low- from high-barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆d in a high-throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast-ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast-ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆d links diverse ion-transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy.
abstract: NA: In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non-fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady-state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited-state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel-type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence-dependent lifetimes (30-200 ps) governed by singlet-singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long-lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin-film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager-like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge-generation mechanisms in Y6-based photovoltaic systems.

title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid-Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics.
abstract: NA: The anchoring group of self-assembled monolayer (SAM) hole-transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21, engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual-action mechanism of pyridine-Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate-metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid-dissociation constants (Ka) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide-bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open-circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all-perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi-dentate pyridine-carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next-generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Breaking the Boltzmann Limit: A Review of Emerging Ultralow-Power Transistor Technologies.
abstract: NA: As complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub-2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub-60 mV/dec steep-switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field-effect transistors (TFETs), negative-capacitance field-effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold-source field-effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub‑60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.

title: Stress-Resistant Plant Cell-Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization.
abstract: NA: Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient-temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold-chain dependence and suppressing solution-phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice-induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress-resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-8) for mechanical support, a water-retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn2 + coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze- and dehydration-driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post-rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra-low protectant content (<5 wt%) together with an ambient shelf-life of at least 3 months, unachievable with previous methods. Furthermore, the rehydrated RBCs preserve their native morphology, membrane mechanics, metabolic activity, oxygen transport capability, and in vivo circulation behavior. This work establishes a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy for transferring desiccation tolerance from plants to mammalian cells, advancing ambient-temperature biostorage of sensitive living systems.

title: Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation-Anion Co-Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes.
abstract: NA: Multivalent cation-anion co-(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge-compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre-intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge-compensation mechanism-organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg2 +-TFSI- as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm- 2 and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm- 2 at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm- 2, surpassing leading Mg-ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co-(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high-performance energy storage.

title: High-Performance Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers via a Tandem Alignment Strategy.
abstract: NA: Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers have shown great potential as shape-memory soft materials due to their large and reversible deformation capacity. However, fabrication methods for LCE fibers with ultrafast thermal response and the exploration of the factors influencing their thermal actuation performance remain limited. A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning is presented to fabricate highly aligned LCE fibers. These LCE fibers achieve an order parameter of up to 0.78 and exhibit exceptional actuation performance under thermal stimulation, including an actuation strain of 80%, an actuation speed of 1485% s-1, and a peak power density of 6105 W kg-1. Furthermore, the actuation performance can be significantly enhanced by resonance. Under constant heating conditions, modulation of the heating frequency enables the actuation speed of the LCE fibers to be amplified up to 10-fold, achieving bioinspired energy efficiency optimization similar to the wing-flapping of insects. The LCE fibers demonstrate promising applicability in scenarios requiring ultrafast and efficient thermal actuation.

title: Tuning N-Species Adsorption/Desorption Equilibrium by Ni1Aun-SrTiO3 for Artificial Urea Photosynthesis.
abstract: NA: Inefficient generation of N-related intermediates, stemming from inert adsorption/photoactivation of N2, has hindered efficient artificial photosynthesis of urea from N2, CO2, and H2O. To overcome this bottleneck, we herein propose a strategy for modulating the adsorption/desorption equilibrium of N-related species using precisely designed bimetallic Ni1Aun active sites supported on a strontium titanate (NiAu-STO) semiconductor photocatalyst. This strategy significantly enhances N2 adsorption/activation and effective generation of N-related intermediates to facilitate C-N coupling for the photocatalytic urea synthesis, affording a considerable urea production rate of 1333.63 µg gcat. -1, with successful crystallization of a collectible solid-phase urea product. Furthermore, we developed a novel reaction-temperature programmed desorption-mass spectrometry tandem monitoring system to elucidate the adsorption behavior of N2, which can clarify the adsorption behavior of N2 and confirm the formation of critical N-related intermediates (e.g., *NH2) on the NiAu-STO photocatalyst. In addition, in situ Raman spectroscopy results further validated the formation of a distinctive C-N coupling intermediate (*NH2COO-) on the photocatalyst surface, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis from N2, CO2, and H2O.

title: Self-Fueling Nanobacteria Harnesses Leaked Pancreatic Fluid to Eradicate Residual Tumors After Surgery.
abstract: NA: Postoperative management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains hindered by two closely linked challenges: the harmful effects of pancreatic fistula and the high risk of local tumor recurrence. Although leaked pancreatic fluid (PF) is generally regarded as a postoperative complication, its abundance of digestive enzymes also suggests an underexplored therapeutic opportunity. Here, we developed a localized therapeutic strategy that converts the enzyme-rich fistula microenvironment from a pathological burden into an antitumor resource. To achieve this, we nano-engineered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B.t.) and integrated it with TRPV1 antagonist-loaded nanomicelles in a GelMA hydrogel, generating the platform TNPs-N@B.t. + Gel. Mechanistically, this system acts in a coordinated manner within the postoperative PDAC microenvironment. B.t. degrades tumor-associated mucins, thereby dismantling the protective barrier that shields PDAC cells from pancreatic enzymes and restoring their vulnerability to enzymatic attack. Meanwhile, PF forms an in situ digestive enzyme corona on the nanoengineered bacterial surface, which promotes deeper tumor penetration by disrupting intercellular adhesion. In parallel, delivery of the TRPV1 antagonist (TRPV1a) suppresses CGRP release, attenuates cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, and facilitates NK-cell-associated antitumor responses. In postoperative PDAC models, TNPs-N@B.t. + Gel showed durable local retention, enhanced tumor accumulation, suppressed recurrence, prolonged survival, and alleviated pain-related behaviors without evident systemic toxicity.

title: Negative-Thermal-Expansion Strategy Enables Hard Carbon With Tuned Heat/Strain Tolerances for Sodium Storage.
abstract: NA: The thermal/stress runaways pose a risk to the safety and industrialization of sodium-ion battery (SIB), which hence requires external management equipment. Actually, the thermal/stress generation originates from the repetitive Na+ intercalation within carbon interlayers and pore-filling in the initial stage. Herein, we propose a regulation strategy of "in situ thermal strain relief" to achieve internal thermal and stress managements of SIB hard carbon (HC) anode by incorporating negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW2O8. The results indicate that the heat and strain were reduced obviously after cycling, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and enhanced sodium storage capacity. Moreover, the microstructure and efficient electron/ion transport within HC were preserved, demonstrating excellent capacity stability even after high-rate and long-term cycling over wide operating temperature ranges (-20°C to 60°C). This study provides a new approach for thermal and stress management inside the battery, which may play a joint effort with the conventional management equipment outside the battery and beyond.

title: Polyacrylate-Based Dielectric Elastomer Fiber Actuators for High-Performance Artificial Muscles.
abstract: NA: Dielectric elastomer fiber actuators (DEFAs) are promising candidates for artificial muscle applications, owing to their high axial actuation and mechanical compliance, yet achieving scalable fabrication without compromising electromechanical performance remains a critical bottleneck. Existing continuous manufacturing routes are predominantly restricted to silicone elastomers, which yield limited actuation strains and low energy densities. Here, a continuous fabrication strategy that integrates coaxial wet spinning with in situ ultraviolet curing is developed to produce polyacrylate-based DEFAs (PA-DEFAs) from a bimodal-networked polyacrylate dielectric elastomer at rates up to 22.5 mm s-1. The fiber geometry and electromechanical properties are readily tunable by adjusting the core-to-shell flow-rate ratio and elastomer formulation. The resulting fiber actuators deliver a maximum prestretch-free axial strain of ∼39%, a maximum energy density of 54.8 J kg- 1, and a peak power density of 443 W kg- 1-outperforming previously reported continuously fabricated DEFAs. The long and continuous fiber architecture further enables wrapped actuator and parallel-connected arrays, facilitating seamless integration into diverse soft robotic systems, including a robotic arm, a crawling robot, and an underwater robotic manta-ray with modular fault-tolerance. By reconciling scalable manufacturing with high actuation performance, PA-DEFAs establish a versatile and manufacturing-compatible platform for next-generation artificial muscles and adaptive soft robotics.

title: Methanesulfonic Acid as a Dual-Role Reagent for Porous Polymer Network Design.
abstract: NA: The need to develop new materials for energy and environmental sustainability has drawn significant attention in recent years due to population growth, depletion of raw materials, and rising costs. Porous materials are at the center of this quest, necessitating facile approaches for their synthesis, as well as for both pristine and post-synthetically modified sorbents. This is crucial to reduce chemical waste and hazards involved in the process. Methanesulfonic acid (MSA) is currently being explored as a reagent for the design and fabrication of porous polymer networks (PPNs), with several successful reports so far in the literature. This perspective highlights the overall properties and benefits of MSA for the design of PPNs. A better understanding of MSA's capabilities will open new frontiers and help overcome the limitations of difficult-to-scale PPNs. This is because although these PPNs are robust, they still suffer major techno-economic setbacks that hinder their integration into industrial processes. In addition to the cost of starting materials, which pose a challenge to commercialization, the synthetic approach also contributes significantly. As MSA can play the role of both a solvent and an acid catalyst in a reaction, it is a promising dual-role reagent for the design of PPNs.

title: Achieving High Spatial Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy Studies in Closed Liquid Cells.
abstract: NA: Liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (LCTEM) is a rising technique for probing dynamic processes and structural transformations in liquid environments at the nanoscale. However, its broader application is largely constrained by limited spatial resolution, which arises from electron scattering by the encapsulating membranes and the liquid layer. Recent advances in instrument design, micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS)-based cells, and ultrathin window materials have substantially improved imaging quality, yet achieving atomic-scale resolution in liquids remains a formidable challenge. This review provides a comprehensive overview of such strategies developed to enhance the spatial resolution of LCTEM, emphasizing the roles of liquid layer thickness, MEMS design, and cell configuration. We highlight representative approaches, such as reducing liquid and membrane thicknesses, optimizing MEMS architectures, and employing grid-based liquid cells, and discuss their underlying mechanisms and recent progress. Finally, we outline current challenges and future opportunities for achieving high-resolution, multifunctional LCTEM systems capable of capturing dynamic processes in realistic liquid environments.

title: Photocatalytic Tandem Reaction for Urea Synthesis From Atmospheric CO2 and N2.
abstract: NA: Photocatalytic urea synthesis directly from atmospheric CO2 and N2 offers a sustainable route to bypass the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process, yet simultaneously achieving CO2 capture and reduction, N2 activation, and C─N coupling within a single system remains challenging. Herein, we report a two-step tandem platform combining ionic-liquid-modified metal-organic framework (IL@PCN-250-Fe2Co) with a trinuclear copper-based covalent organic framework (HTP-Cu3-imi-COF) for urea photosynthesis from air. The IL@MOF captures atmospheric CO2 and photoreduces it to CO, while HTP-Cu3-imi-COF couples the generated CO with ambient N2 into urea. This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·gcat -1·h-1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO2 and N2. In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole-functionalized HTP segments act as hole-rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu3 clusters serve as electron-rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.

title: Cation-Framework-Preserving Oxygen-Vacancy Engineering for Broadband Infrared Emission in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides.
abstract: NA: High-temperature radiative ceramics require broadband infrared emission and stable structures, but the defects that enhance emission can also weaken oxide lattices. Here, we regulate oxygen vacancies in (MnCrFeNiCu)3O4, a high-entropy spinel oxide (HEO), by vacuum annealing without changing the nominal cation composition. This approach regulates oxygen nonstoichiometry without introducing an additional cation-substitution variable. The binary Mn-Cr reference has band-averaged emissivities of 0.668 and 0.726 over 0.78-2.5 and 2.5-16 µm, respectively. Pristine HEO increases these values to 0.919 and 0.863, while the optimized HEO-OV-5 h reaches 0.932 and 0.902. Multication incorporation broadens electronic states near the band edges. Oxygen removal creates vacancy-derived states, redistributes charge, and changes local M─O coordination. The vacancy-derived states are consistent with localized d-d excitation, intervalence charge transfer, and polaron-related absorption, while changes in M─O coordination broaden vibrational absorption. Together, these electronic and local structural changes are consistent with the enhanced infrared emissivity. The spinel framework and high emissivity remain largely preserved after annealing at 1000°C for 5 h. These results show that oxygen vacancies can be regulated within a stable multication spinel to combine broadband infrared emission with high-temperature stability.

title: "Water-in-Water" Biphasic Electrolyte for Aqueous Zinc-ion Batteries.
abstract: NA: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn2+ transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn2+ flux can instead be regulated by aqueous-aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous "water-in-water" (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)-rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)-rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn2+ accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm-2 and 10 mAh cm-2, and Ah-level Zn||NaV3O8 pouch cells sustain long-term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn2+ transport.

title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery-Type Operation: A Re-Functionalized Ti-MOF for Solar Energy Storage.
abstract: NA: Efficient harvesting, storage, and on-demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy-driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti-based bipyridine MOF, COK47-bpy, and its ReCl(CO)3-functionalized analogue, ReCl47-bpy, as photochargeable materials for time-decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and "electron sink" sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible-light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47-bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g-1 MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H2) evolution with electron-to-H2 efficiencies exceeding 90%.
