Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO-supported layers, ReCl47-bpy|FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g-1 MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re-functionalized Ti-MOFs as versatile platforms for solar-driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF-based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next-generation MOF-based energy devices.

title: Cyclic Nonequilibrium Processing of Halide Solid Electrolytes for Low-Pressure Operation of all-Solid-State Batteries.
abstract: NA: Sluggish ionic transport and high rigidity of inorganic solid electrolytes (SSEs) necessitate ultra-high external pressures in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), posing a major barrier to their deployment. Herein, we propose a cyclic nonequilibrium thermal process for Li3InCl6 (LIC) solid electrolyte, which is implemented through repeated quenching to concurrently optimize ionic transport and deformability. The initial quench refines particle size, whereas subsequent quenching induces local amorphization, thereby suppressing grain boundary resistance and enhancing compressibility. Meanwhile, additional Li vacancies are introduced, accelerating bulk phase ionic transport. These coupled mesoscopic and microscopic structural evolutions increase the room-temperature ionic conductivity (IC) of LIC from 1.3 to 6.8 mS/cm, while reducing the Young's modulus from 42.3 to 17.6 GPa. The optimized LIC enables a stable cycling of ASSBs at a low operation pressure of 2 MPa with a high areal capacity of 7.7 mAh/cm2, highlighting cyclic nonequilibrium processing as a promising route for practical ASSBs.

title: Advances in Bio-Integrated Edge Computing Systems for Smart and Connected Health.
abstract: NA: Recent advances in bio-integrated healthcare technologies have enabled continuous, high-resolution monitoring and active therapeutic intervention through wearable, implantable, and ingestible platforms. In parallel, edge computing has emerged as a critical framework for processing biomedical data locally, enabling low-latency, energy-efficient, and privacy-preserving operation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bio-integrated edge computing systems for smart and connected health, focusing on the co-design of computing, sensing, and energy strategies. We first examine computing approaches, including conventional von Neumann architectures and emerging paradigms such as compute-in-memory and neuromorphic systems, for on-device data processing and decision-making. We then discuss sensing strategies that enhance signal fidelity and enable efficient information representation at the biointerface. Finally, we review energy solutions that enable continuous, autonomous operation. By integrating these domains, this work outlines pathways toward scalable, adaptive, and fully autonomous edge healthcare systems.

title: Rare-Earth-Cluster-Mediated Long-Range Electronic Modulation Activates Zn Atomic Sites for Oxygen Reduction Catalysis.
abstract: NA: Activating the inert Zn (d10) centers via precise ligand-field engineering to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance is highly appealing yet challenging. Herein, we report a general long-range electronic structure regulation strategy to construct ultrafine rare-earth oxide clusters anchored proximal to Zn single-atom sites (LaOx-Zn-SA/CNCl), aiming at boosting ORR activity. Benefiting from the tailored long-range electronic modulation by LaOx clusters and the hierarchical porous carbon support that maximizes Zn atom utilization, the catalysts exhibit a high half-wave potential of 0.90 V along with remarkable stability in alkaline media. This represents a non-precious-metal, rare-earth-based electrocatalyst among the best reported so far. A zinc-air battery (ZAB) integrating LaOx-Zn-SA/CNCl as the cathode catalyst delivers a maximum power density of 177.3 mW cm-2 at 225 mA cm-2. Theoretical calculations reveal that the proximal LaOx clusters remotely modulate the electronic structures of Zn sites, enhancing electron-transfer efficiency by strengthening electronic interactions. With the optimized electronic state of Zn sites, the adsorption of key intermediates is balanced to alleviate the energy barriers of the rate-determining step. This work provides insights into the long-range electronic regulation of transition-metal single-atom sites within a hierarchical rare-earth cluster-coupled microenvironment for efficient electrocatalysis.

title: Hypoxia-Tolerant Supramolecular Nanomicelles for Pyroptosis-Enhanced NIR-II Phototheranostics.
abstract: NA: Tumor hypoxia, limited solid-tumor imaging, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity remain major challenges to effective cancer phototheranostics. Here, a molecular conformation engineering strategy is developed to construct TBBP, which features a strengthened electron donor, a moderately twisted conformation, extended π-conjugation, and a robust molecular skeleton free of labile olefinic π-bridges. TBBP exhibits excellent photostability, broadband second near-infrared (1000-1600 nm) emission, and efficient photothermal conversion (42.17%). Supramolecular assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 affords stable TBBP nanomicelles, TBBP NPs, that selectively generate superoxide radicals (O2 -•) and retain potent Type I photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity under hypoxia. Photoactivated TBBP NPs further induce mitochondrial dysfunction and caspase-3/GSDME-mediated immunogenic pyroptosis, promoting dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell infiltration. In a bilateral 4T1 tumor model, TBBP NPs enable high-contrast second near-infrared (NIR-II) imaging, while synergistic Type I PDT and photothermal therapy elicit systemic antitumor immunity, achieving 92.0% primary tumor inhibition and 47.7% distant tumor inhibition. This work establishes a molecular conformation engineering strategy and extends its functionality through supramolecular assembly, synergistically integrating NIR-II imaging, hypoxia-tolerant Type I phototherapy, and photoimmunotherapy, thereby providing a generalizable molecular design principle for the development of next-generation multifunctional organic phototheranostic agents.

title: Boundary Guided Liquid-Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick-and-Release.
abstract: NA: Liquid-bridge-mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid-bridge formation and retraction under non-ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid-bridge adhesion strategy using a two-tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary-guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid-bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload-free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage-free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid-bridge-based robotic end effector for pick-and-place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra-gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.

title: High-Performance Low Threshold Voltage n-Type OECTs via a Stepwise Cyanation of Quinoxaline-Based Polymeric Semiconductor.
abstract: NA: Achieving both low threshold voltage (Vth) and high performance in organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) is critical for low-power, high-sensitivity bioelectronics, yet simultaneously achieving low Vth and high device performance remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, we propose a stepwise cyanation strategy to modify quinoxaline-based polymeric semiconductors to mitigate this dilemma. Benefiting from the strong electron-withdrawing ability of cyano substituents, QxCN-CNTVT functionalized with cyano groups on both donor and acceptor units exhibits a deep LUMO level of -4.23 eV, one of the deepest among reported n-type ionic-electronic conductors. As a result, OECTs based on QxCN-CNTVT demonstrate excellent comprehensive performance, with a high µC* value of up to 168.89 F cm-1 V-1 s-1 and a low Vth of 0.13 V, while maintaining superior operational stability (retaining ∼80% of the initial current after 10,000 s of continuous operation and 10,000 full switching cycles). Furthermore, QxCN-CNTVT is successfully applied to complementary inverters for efficient amplification of electrooculogram (EOG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, as well as NAND and NOR logic gates for integrated logic functions. This work not only alleviates the widely observed imbalance between performance and Vth in n-type OECTs but also provides a versatile molecular design strategy for next-generation low-power bioelectronic devices.

title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal-Bacteria Interactions.
abstract: NA: The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever-increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations. To make these recommendations operational, we provide a source-specific experimental roadmap, identify priority mechanistic questions with concrete investigation pathways, and highlight representative studies that combine causal perturbations, orthogonal measurements, and cross-laboratory validation.

title: Layered Spin-Crossover Metal-Organic Frameworks for Light-Induced Control of Two-Dimensional Quantum Materials.
abstract: NA: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann-type spin-crossover (SCO) MOF {FeII(pyS2Et)2[PtII(CN)4]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two-dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli-responsive nature of SCO-layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few-layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe2) through the strain induced via thermal and light-induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin-valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non-volatile zero-field memory. In NbSe2, light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli-responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain-mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF-based architectures beyond traditional porous-matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.

title: Directional Confinement Governed Ion Transport for Efficient Actuation.
abstract: NA: Ionic transport kinetics in electrolytes are a key determinant of ionic actuator performance. Conventional random porous electrolytes are constrained by porosity and tortuosity, leading to an intrinsic limitation in ion mobility within the Bruggeman framework. Here, structural anisotropy is introduced to establish a unified framework that analyzes ion transport from random diffusion to directionally confined regimes. To validate this concept, anisotropic electrolytes with oriented channels are fabricated via directional freeze-drying. These structures exhibit pronounced directional dependence, with through-plane ion mobility twice higher than that of the disordered counterparts, leading to significantly enhanced ionic actuator performance and mitigating the inherent trade-off between strain and blocking force. Moreover, the directional confinement effect is observed across multiple polymer systems, highlighting the critical role of structural anisotropy in regulating ion transport and offering a framework for enhancing electrolyte performance through microstructural design. This strategy enables environmentally robust and stable operation of soft electrochemical actuators for grippers and biomimetic robotics.

title: Dual Twisted Interfaces Enable Tunable Second Harmonic Generation in Chemical Vapor Deposition Grown Trilayer MoS2.
abstract: NA: Twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, governed by a single twisted interface, offer a versatile platform for manipulating interlayer coupling and emergent optical behavior. However, despite extensive studies on single twisted interface systems, how multi-interface twisted stacking influences nonlinear optical behavior remains unclear. Here, we address this gap by systematically investigating the nonlinear optical performance of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown twisted trilayer MoS2 (TT-MoS2) with multi-interface twisted stacking. We fabricate all nine distinct trilayer MoS2 configurations by CVD. Raman and photoluminescence show that twisted interfaces modulate interlayer coupling, giving rise to stacking-dependent phonon and excitonic responses. Atomic-resolution scanning, transmission electron microscopy, and selected area electron diffraction confirm dual twisted interfaces and a supermoiré lattice. Guided by these structural insights, we examine the second harmonic generation (SHG) response across all nine trilayer configurations. Extending the coherent SH field superposition model to a trilayer system with two independent twisted interfaces, we develop a framework that describes how the dual interfaces govern the SHG intensity and polarization orientation across stacking configurations. Our findings establish TT-MoS2 as a versatile nonlinear platform and open new avenues for understanding and exploiting multi-interface twisted coupling to engineer nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals materials.

title: Solvation-Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide-Temperature Operation of High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries.
abstract: NA: High-energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep-sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature-sensitive ion transport, Li+ solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation-equilibrium-locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low-freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr13DFOB (1-methyl-1-propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic-liquid co-solvent. Cooperative ion-dipole and weak C-H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr13 + regulate the free-solvent reservoir, while TFSI- (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB- enrich the primary Li+ coordination shell. Variable-temperature 7Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent-separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from -60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature-responsive Pyr13DFOB-free electrolyte. This locked anion-rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li+, mitigates solvent-derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF- and borate-rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811. Consequently, Li||NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at -85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to -122.9°C. A 6.6 Ah Li||Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg-1 under lean-electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation-equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range.

title: Thickness-Defined Transport Regime Toward Near-Ideal Area-Type Switching.
abstract: NA: Area-type memristors are attractive for analog in-memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non-pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near-ideal area-type switching emerges within a tunneling-governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging-related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta2O5/Pt in a range of 3-10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near-short-circuit transport with two gradual-switching modes with different readout stability. The 5-6 nm thickness window suppresses non-pinched hysteresis and short-time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity-symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near-linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap-assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized-state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine-state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi-static I-V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse-width-dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog-A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime-defining design rule for near-ideal area-type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi-state memristors for in-memory computing applications.

title: Synthesis of Bulk Superconducting LiNbO2 Crystals Through CaH2 Reduction.
abstract: NA: We have synthesized layered superconducting LiNbO2 crystals through a bulk phase transformation from LiNbO3 single crystals via CaH2 reduction. As the Nb valence is reduced from 5+ to 3+, the material undergoes a structural transformation to the resulting product, LiNbO2, which is accompanied by metallic behavior and a superconducting transition, Tc onset, as high as 14.4 K. Secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) show that the resulting phase is hole-doped through de-lithiation during the reduction. Magnetization and AC susceptibility measurements from a tunnel diode resonator confirm the bulk nature of superconductivity with a superconducting volume fraction of ≈77% and an upper critical field approaching 26 T. Our study demonstrates extreme hydride reduction as an effective method to induce phase transformations with non-topochemical pathways and can be used to synthesize bulk materials with exotic properties.

title: Voltage Hysteresis Induced by Fragile Quasi-Flat Bands in Oxygen-Redox Cathodes.
abstract: NA: Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg-1. However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long-standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi-flat-band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long-standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation-driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi-flat-band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen-redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.

title: Axial Benzotriazole-Coordinated Ni Single Atoms Enable Rapid Interfacial Electron Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Acetylene Semi-Hydrogenation.
abstract: NA: Photocatalytic semi-hydrogenation of acetylene (C2H2) to ethylene (C2H4) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C2H2. Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C3N4 (BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4) facilitates interfacial electron-transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA-coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d-band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C2H2. Consequently, BTA-Ni SAs-C3N4 achieves a very high C2H4 production rate of 32.29 mmol gcat -1 h-1 with a C2H4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4-times higher than that for Ni SAs-C3N4. The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi-hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance photocatalysts.

title: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation.
abstract: NA: Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (ηeff/Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi-level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid-infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding ηeff/Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large‑scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate‑driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.

title: Correction to "Screening Natural Cholesterol Analogs to Assemble Self-Adjuvant Lipid Nanoparticles for Antigens Tagging Guided Therapeutic Tumor Vaccine".
Synchronized Ablation of Multifocal Tumors Enabled by Multi-Channel Lanthanide Nanocomposites.
abstract: NA: The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi-channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH-responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione-responsive near-infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature-responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole-body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.

title: Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics: From Anatomical Access to Disease-Focused Applications.
abstract: NA: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation-mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter-based, ocular, or intra-articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site-specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease-focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth-factor supplementation, local antibody-fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat-dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.

title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation-Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors.
abstract: NA: Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect-mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path-dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles (n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full-cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation-mediated nucleation and orientation-regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.

title: Nonreciprocal Bending in Ferroelectric Membranes Driven by Flexoelectricity.
abstract: NA: Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi-static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single-crystalline PbTiO3 membrane using suspended-membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity-dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase-field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.

title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion-Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells.
abstract: NA: Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate-phase film with a Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two-step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums-based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1-sun illumination (ISOS-L-2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.

title: All-In-One Integration of Inherently Flame-Retardant, UV-Resistant, and Antibacterial Polymer by a Biguanide Unit.
abstract: NA: The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra-efficient strategy to achieve the all-in-one integration of inherently flame-retardant, UV-resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high-temperature char-formation for flame retardance, n→π* transition absorption for UV-resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide-containing polymer material achieves the best UL-94 V-0 flame-retardant rating with excellent self-extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra-high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely-existed bacteria.

title: Magnetic-Field-Annealing-Induced Short-Range Order in High-Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response.
abstract: NA: The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO-supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of -72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature-specific maxima. Local microscopy, field-associated atomistic modeling, and fixed-composition electronic-structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co-centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.

title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium-Free Acidic Water Oxidation.
abstract: NA: The pursuit of noble metal-free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity-stability trade-off, wherein non-precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium-stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu0.08Co2.92O4) designed through site-specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu-O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co-O covalency and suppresses Co2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co-Co distance to favor direct O-O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu0.08Co2.92O4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm-2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm-2, highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: An Ultrarobust Dual-Modal Neural Fiber With In-Sensor Computing.
abstract: NA: Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human-machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in-sensor-computing dual-modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness-sustaining 300 times load-bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in-sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real-time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material-architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual-modality, and in-sensor computing, setting the stage for next-generation wearable human-machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.

title: Turning Nd-Fe-B Swarf Into High-Value Bulk Feedstocks via Sustainable Hydrogen Plasma: From Rare-Earth Oxides to Metals and Hydrides.
abstract: NA: Rare-earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and other high-efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy-intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare-earth elements (REEs) content (∼20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we achieve phase separation into metallic Fe and a Nd2O3-rich rare-earth fraction, providing a concentrated intermediate for subsequent REPM production. The process also enables direct rare-earth hydride formation, confirming the plasma-assisted partial rare-earth metallization in the molten state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high-value, high-purity feedstock in a single, acid-free step. Against the ∼70 kg CO2-eq kg-1 footprint of conventional REPM production, this recycling route offers a pathway toward substantially lower-emission magnet production while reducing reliance on primary REE supply.

title: A Universal Spin-Polarization-Engineered Antibonding-Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh-Rate Sodium-Ion Batteries.
abstract: NA: Conversion-type anode materials hold great promise for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass-transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal-chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long-standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin-polarization-engineered (SPE) antibonding-orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh-rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin-state transition from low-spin to high-spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal eg orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin-engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn-FeS2/CoS2 anode delivers an ultrahigh-rate capability of 300 mA h g-1 at 120 A g-1, together with exceptional long-term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g-1), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial-level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.

title: Nonlinear Electro-Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid-State Quantum Defects.
abstract: NA: Integrated visible photonic engines for solid-state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt-scale visible light generation and high-contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip-scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high-fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz-bandwidth electro-optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off-chip green-light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time-resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time-tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high-speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high-rate quantum communication nodes.

title: Hydrogel adhesives with phase-transition-regulated tough wet adhesion and gentle removal for hemorrhage treatment and wound closure.
abstract: NA: Hydrogel bioadhesives featuring rapid and robust wet adhesion are promising for hemorrhage and wound management. Nevertheless, the tight linkage may lead to secondary injury during surgical operations for subsequent removal. Herein, we develop an advanced hydrogel (PANA) with adequate wet adhesion performance (adhesion strength of 61.2 ± 9 kPa and interfacial toughness of 523 ± 36 J m-2) at body temperature and facile removal properties (adhesion strength of 5.3 ± 2.2 kPa and interfacial toughness of 50 ± 7 J m-2) at 20 °C. The main mechanism is the involvement of N-acryloyl-L-phenylalanine in hydrogel network, which not only realizes interfacial drainage and enhances matrix cohesion owing to the unique coupling structure of carboxylic and phenyl groups but also promotes thermo-triggered phase transition through regulation of hydrogen-bond-mediated hydrophobic aggregation with N-isopropylacrylamide. PANA hydrogel achieves instantaneous hemostatic sealing of diverse injuries in rabbits, and spraying normal saline (20 °C) promotes fast phase separation to enable gentle detachment for the prevention of secondary damage. Combined with cold plasma activation, the hydrogel inhibits bacterial proliferation to accelerate infected skin wound healing. Our work provides a practical solution to address the dilemma of tight wet adhesion and on-demand removal by clinically-used adhesives.

title: Ultrasound-programmable poly(amino acid) nanocomposite enables synchronized metal ion-cisplatin release to overcome multidrug resistance.
abstract: NA: Although immunotherapy has demonstrated remarkable clinical anti-cancer efficacy, chemotherapy remains the most widely used therapeutic modality. Multidrug resistance (MDR) remains a major barrier to platinum-based chemotherapy and is closely associated with insufficient intracellular drug accumulation, elevated antioxidant capacity, and impaired stress responsiveness in cancer cells. Here, an ultrasound (US)-programmable poly(amino acid) nanocomposite, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP, is developed to enable synchronized intracellular release of Fe(II) and cisplatin (CDDP) for coordinated chemoresistance reversal. Under US irradiation, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP accelerates the release of Fe(II) and CDDP in tumor microenvironments (TMEs), triggering overproduction of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and amplifying oxidative stress. In CDDP-resistant A549DDP lung caner cells, EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP elevates ROS levels by 2.7-fold and reduces glutathione (GSH) levels to 31.2% of those in the Control group. Further mechanistic investigation reveals that the robust intracellular oxidative stress and associated mitochondrial damage also enhance autophagic activity, as evidenced by a marked increase in autolysosome formation. EG-KFc20-KSA/CDDP combined with US achieves an 85.3% tumor inhibition rate and prolongs the survival of A549DDP tumor-bearing mice to 61 days in vivo. This study establishes a US-programmable metal ion/chemotherapeutic co-delivery strategy that integrates oxidative stress amplification with chemotherapy and provides a mechanistically supported strategy for overcoming MDR.

title: Nose-to-brain delivery of multimodal nanoregulator restores metal-redox homeostasis and protects mitochondrial integrity for triple inhibitions of neuronal death in radiation-induced brain injury.
abstract: NA: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) has emerged as a severe complication of cranial radiotherapy, substantially impairing patients' quality of life. Current therapies mainly rely on anti-apoptotic drugs with limited efficacy. Despite advances in understanding neuronal death in RIBI, efficient neuroprotective strategies are still lacking. Herein, we identify that beyond apoptosis, neuronal ferroptosis and cuproptosis are key drivers of RIBI. To simultaneously inhibit all three death pathways, unlike traditional approach based on small-molecular inhibitors and their combinations, we propose an innovative strategy to disrupt the vicious cycle of ROS/Fe3+/Cu2+ overload and mitochondrial dysfunction that co-drive the three cell death modalities. And a therapeutic nanodot (SPDA-SeMet) is facilely engineered by conjugating natural selenomethionine onto small-sized polydopamine nanoparticles. In RIBI mice, therapeutic outcome of SPDA-SeMet significantly outperforms neuroprotective comparator Edaravone/Dexborneol. Mechanistically, negatively-charged surface and ultrasmall size enable rapid mucus penetration and enhanced nose-to-brain delivery, and then SPDA and SeMet modules work together to restore ROS/Fe3+/Cu2+ homeostasis and preserve mitochondrial integrity in neurons via enhanced capacity in Fe3+/Cu2+ chelation, ROS scavenging, mitochondrial colocalization, thereby efficiently inhibiting neuronal apoptosis/ferroptosis/cuproptosis and inflammation. Our findings establish an essential role of neuronal ferroptosis/cuproptosis/apoptosis in RIBI pathogenesis, and provides a therapeutic nanoplatform regulating complex pathological processes for targeted therapy.

title: First use of a woven allogeneic vascular graft made of cell-assembled extracellular matrix (CAM) as an arteriovenous shunt in sheep: a pilot study.
abstract: NA: Reliable vascular access is vital for patients undergoing hemodialysis. Current arteriovenous shunts (AVS) made of expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) are prone to thrombosis, intimal hyperplasia, and infections. To overcome these limitations, biological Tissue-Engineered Vascular Grafts (TEVGs) were produced by weaving threads made from Cell-Assembled extracellular Matrix (CAM), i.e., extracellular matrix produced by ovine fibroblasts in culture. The woven TEVGs were designed with a 6 mm internal diameter and beveled ends to facilitate use as an AVS. They had a burst pressure (3069 ± 546 mmHg) and a compliance (4.4 ± 0.5%/100 mmHg) closer to those of native blood vessels than ePTFE prostheses. Woven TEVGs were implanted as carotid-jugular AVS in sheep and compared to ePTFE controls in a bilateral model (n = 8 animals). Grafts were easily punctured with 16G hemodialysis needles once at 4 weeks without loss of structural integrity or hemorrhagic complications. Overall TEVGs patency was 100%, while it was 87.5% for ePTFE grafts (n = 8). Histological analysis revealed an inflammatory response that decreased between 4 and 8 weeks. A luminal neotissue was observed at 8 weeks with smooth muscle cells and localized endothelialization. Localized calcification of CAM was observed and appeared to be correlated with high tissue compaction. This proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of using a completely biological TEVG made from woven CAM as an AVS in an allogeneic large animal model. Future studies are needed to understand and avoid the never-before-observed calcification of the CAM in a large animal model, as well as to determine longer-term outcomes.

title: Bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactors suppress lung cancer stem-like cells by triggering a self-amplifying endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria stress loop.
abstract: NA: The compensatory signal transmission between the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria maintains the survival of lung cancer stem cells (LCSCs). This study designed a bio-orthogonally functionalized biomimetic nanoreactor to dissociate this protective crosstalk and induce a self-amplifying stress feedback loop. By integrating an N-cadherin-targeting aptamer with tumor membrane masking technology, this nanoreactor achieves enhanced specificity for LCSCs targeting. The nanoreactor is loaded with the photosensitizer TAPP and bortezomib (BTZ). Upon laser irradiation, TAPP generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) locally, rapidly collapsing the mitochondrial membrane potential and inducing oxidative injury. Concurrently, BTZ inhibits the proteasome, blocking the degradation of ubiquitinated proteins and triggering acute ER stress, which promotes Ca2+ release into mitochondria and further exacerbates mitochondrial damage. In turn, damaged mitochondria release mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), aggravating ER dysfunction and establishing a self-amplifying vicious cycle between the ER and mitochondria that progressively escalates cellular damage. Additionally, treatment was accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and decreased expression of stemness-associated markers, alongside ER-mitochondrial dysfunction and enhanced cytotoxicity in stem-like cells.

title: FGF2-engineered extracellular vesicles loaded in an ECM-mimetic hydrogel promote wound healing and attenuate scar formation via immunomodulation and enhanced neurovascular responses.
abstract: NA: Impaired wound healing in diabetes is primarily driven by persistent inflammation and neurovascular dysfunction, frequently leading to aberrant tissue remodeling and pathological scarring. Extracellular vesicles of adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADSC-EVs) have therapeutic potential but limited tissue-specific efficacy. Fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) promotes angiogenesis and nerve repair but suffers from a short half-life that limits its clinical application. Given the low endogenous expression of FGF2 in ADSCs and its short half-life in vivo, here, we engineered FGF2-functionalized EVs (EV-FGF2) by lentiviral transduction of ADSCs and incorporated them into a click chemistry-crosslinked recombinant collagen/hyaluronic acid hydrogel (CH/EV-FGF2) to enable sustained release and extracellular matrix-mimetic support. In vitro, EV-FGF2 promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative M2 phenotype, enhanced angiogenesis and axonal outgrowth. In vivo, the CH/EV-FGF2 hydrogel accelerated wound closure in a diabetic mouse wound model, attenuated early inflammation, increased vascular (CD31) and neuronal (βIII-tubulin/Tuj1) markers, promoted neurovascular-associated responses, and attenuated scar formation in a rabbit ear model. In conclusion, this study developed an engineered EV-FGF2 hydrogel system that addresses multiple pathological aspects of diabetic wounds, offering a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for tissue repair.

title: Spatial bridges of hierarchical scaffolds orchestrate MSCs/SCs interaction for bone regeneration.
abstract: NA: The spatiotemporal distribution of multiple cells and their interactions with extracellular matrix in three-dimensional microenvironments play a critical role in regulating cell behaviors and modulating tissue development and regeneration. Preparation of hierarchical structural scaffolds for multicellular crosstalk in tissue engineering holds great significance. Here, inspired conceptually by the idea of "magpie bridge", biomimetic hierarchical multi-channel scaffolds, serving as "spatial bridges" to orchestrate multicellular spatiotemporal interactions have been proposed for innervated bone regeneration. Hierarchical multi-channel structures facilitate the mutual migration and energy metabolism activities of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and Schwann cells (SCs), thereby enhancing their specific differentiation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that MSCs/SCs cross-talk mediated by cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, including the activation of multiple neurogenesis/osteogenesis-related signaling pathways. In rabbit bone defect model, SCs-laden hierarchical multi-channel scaffolds constructed a neuro-inductive metabolism-activated microenvironment, thereby achieving 3.24-fold increase in bone regeneration and 2.29-fold increase in neuro-vascular networks reconstruction compared to traditional bioceramic scaffolds in the core defects region at 12-week post-surgery, respectively. Therefore, this study introduces an exceptional concept that biomimetic hierarchical scaffolds serve as "spatial bridges" for accelerating multicellular spatiotemporal interactions of complex tissue and organ regeneration, opening new avenues for designing next-generation regenerative biomaterials.

title: Charge-neutralized anti-swelling hydrogels enable mechano-curvature-coupled microphysiological system.
abstract: NA: Curvature topography and mechanical stimulation are key biophysical cues in the tissue microenvironment that play critical roles in regulating cell behavior. However, the stable construction of curved structures and the application of dynamic mechanical loading in ultrasoft biomaterials remain challenging, limiting the reconstruction of microenvironments for soft tissues such as the lung. Here, we propose a charge-neutralization anti-swelling hydrogel strategy. By introducing LiCl, Li+ ions electrostatically shield and coordinate with fixed negative charges, thereby suppressing the Donnan effect to inhibit hydrogel swelling and enhance structural stability. The resulting hydrogel exhibits a tunable Young's modulus ranging from 1.12 to 339.79 kPa. Combined with three-dimensional (3D) printing, biomimetic curved structures with curvatures ranging from 10-4 to 4 × 10-2 μm-1 were stably fabricated. Integration with a stretching driver further enabled controllable cyclic stretching (0∼40%), establishing a microphysiological system that couples curvature topography with mechanical cues and recapitulates the physiological and pathological parameters of multiple tissues. Curvature topography and mechanical stimulation significantly influenced tissue phenotypes, including surfactant secretion, proliferation, and migration, as well as drug sensitivity. This work provides a general design strategy for reconstructing complex tissue microenvironments and establishes a more physiologically relevant platform for investigating tissue development, disease mechanisms, and drug responses.

title: Heptamethine cyanines serve as photocaged Michael electrophiles for spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis immunotherapy.
abstract: NA: Inhibiting glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) to induce ferroptosis has emerged as a crucial strategy to circumvent drug resistance. However, conventional GPX4 inhibitors, typically α-chloroacetamides, show limitations in the stability and targetability required for drug development. Here we uncover that heptamethine cyanines (Cy7) function as photocaged Michael electrophiles, enabling spatiotemporal GPX4 inhibition and ferroptosis induction with submicromolar to nanomolar potencies against both parental and drug-resistant cancer cells. The strong phototoxicity originates from the optimized electrophilicity window of the photo-uncaged Michael electrophiles, which enables selective alkylation of GPX4 selenocysteine over glutathione (GSH), thereby circumventing cellular GSH detoxification. Furthermore, the structural tunability of Cy7 dyes enables on-demand fabrication of cancer cell-specific GPX4 inhibitors, as exemplified by an enzyme-activatable Cy7 prodrug that selectively killed cancer cells in primary tumors under photoirradiation while eliciting systemic antitumor immunity to suppress distant tumors. This work establishes a new paradigm for GPX4 inhibitor development and repurposes conventional Cy7 imaging scaffolds as anticancer agents.

title: Energy band tunable piezoelectric nanozyme heterojunction toward cancer synergistic catalytic therapy.
abstract: NA: Piezoelectric catalytic therapy (PCT) based on piezoelectric semiconductors provides a new approach for cancer therapy. Various researches have explored the construction of heterojunction structures with nanozymes to strengthen PCT effect via accelerating electron transfer kinetics and synergistic nanozyme catalysis therapy (NCT). However, limited by the fixed energy band structure of nanozymes, the selectable piezoelectric semiconductors and nanozymes with matched energy levels are few. In this work, Cu2+ engineered nanozyme MIL-100 (Fe) was self-assembled on the surface of piezoelectric material BaTiO3 (BTO) to obtain BaTiO3@MIL-100 (Fe, Cu) (BTO@Fe-Cu) nanoparticles (NPs) with flexible heterojunction types, which presented synergetic NCT and PCT effect. Theoretical calculations revealed that Cu2+ introduced a new 3d orbital in the Fe-O structure, which altered the charge transfer pathways and enhanced the dual-enzyme activity of MIL-100 (Fe). Lattice distortion further modulated the valence band gap and transformed the heterostructure from type-Ⅰ to type-S for high electron-hole separation efficiency. BTO@Fe-Cu NPs fundamentally intensified the efficiency of NCT and PCT, which synergistically activated the ferroptosis/cuproptosis pathways. Moreover, scRNA-seq analysis indicated treatment-associated changes in immune-cell composition and transcriptional states. Together with the immunophenotyping results, these findings supported the potential of the piezoelectric nanozyme for the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) regulation.

title: Polysaccharide-confined polyaniline nanocomplexes reprogram pyrimidine metabolism for synergistic photothermal tumor ablation.
abstract: NA: Polyaniline (PANI) is a promising near-infrared (NIR) photothermal agent, yet its aggregation propensity and lack of intrinsic metabolic regulatory functions restrict its in vivo antitumor application. To overcome these limitations, we engineered a biocompatible curdlan/fucoidan/polyaniline (CFP) ternary inclusion complex via a nanoconfined in-situ polymerization strategy. Utilizing the hydrophobic helical cavity of curdlan as a nano-reactor effectively regulates PANI chain growth, yielding monodispersed nanorods with superior aqueous dispersion stability. Fucoidan serves a dual role as an efficient dispersant and a potent metabolic modulator implicated in pyrimidine pathway suppression. Mechanistically, CFP enters lung adenocarcinoma cells predominantly via macropinocytosis, accounting for ∼44-47% of total internalization, with clathrin- and caveolae-mediated routes contributing only marginally. Multi-omics profiling reveals that fucoidan preferentially modulates pyrimidine metabolism, with significant down-regulation of the core enzymes TK1, DTYMK, and CDA observed at both transcriptomic and protein levels. This metabolic suppression compromises DNA damage repair capacity, rendering the massive ROS accumulation and severe DNA damage induced by PANI-based photothermal therapy largely irreversible and achieving remarkable synergistic antitumor efficacy. Bioinformatic analysis further links these metabolic genes to T cell exhaustion and immune microenvironment remodeling. In vivo, the CFP + NIR regimen exhibits prominent tumor accumulation, potent growth inhibition, and prolonged survival. Crucially, comprehensive toxicological assessments in immunocompetent mice-including hematological, serum biochemical, and histological analyses-confirm the excellent systemic biosafety of CFP. This work presents a promising strategy coupling natural polysaccharide-mediated metabolic intervention with photothermal ablation for precise tumor therapy.

title: Use of a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate for efficient therapy in both primary and metastatic uveal melanoma.
abstract: NA: Uveal melanoma (UM), the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, is associated with a high risk of metastasis, recurrence, and irreversible vision loss. However, current therapeutic options remain limited by insufficient efficacy and poor vision preservation. Building upon the molecular design of SL1-MMAE, a c-Met-targeting aptamer-drug conjugate (ApDC), here we investigate its potential translational application as a targeted therapeutic strategy for both primary and metastatic UM. SL1-MMAE exhibits high binding specificity, rapid cellular internalization, and potent cytotoxicity toward UM cells in vitro. In vivo, SL1-MMAE effectively suppresses tumor growth in both subcutaneous xenograft and liver metastasis models, significantly prolonging survival. Notably, in an orthotopic intraocular UM model, a single intravitreal injection of SL1-MMAE induces robust tumor regression without detectable ocular toxicity at the therapeutic dose. The small molecular size of the ApDC enables superior tumor penetration and reduced retention from non-target ocular tissues. These features are particularly advantageous within the confined intraocular environment, leading to enhanced therapeutic efficacy with improved safety. Compared with the clinically advanced c-Met antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) ABBV-399, the ApDC demonstrates superior antitumor activity and ocular biocompatibility for intraocular UM therapy. Nevertheless, as a preclinical study, further safety, pharmacokinetic and translational studies are warranted to better define the clinical potential of SL1-MMAE. Collectively, these findings establish c-Met-targeting ApDCs as a promising platform for the treatment of both primary and metastatic UM, offering a vision-preserving therapeutic strategy with potent antitumor efficacy and favorable safety profiles.

title: Endothelium-targeted myc silencing suppresses pathological ocular neovascularization.
abstract: NA: Ocular neovascularization (NV) causes blindness, yet anti-VEGF therapy has limited efficacy. Myc controls endothelial cell (EC) proliferation and activation, however, its pathological role in ocular NV and therapeutic value remain unclear. In this study, we found that Myc was markedly upregulated in neovascular ECs (NV-ECs). Mechanistically, glycolytic reprogramming drove the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP), promoting Myc O-GlcNAcylation, which stabilized Myc protein. Endothelial-specific Myc knockout significantly suppressed EC proliferation, thereby alleviating NV progression and preserving visual function. To target Myc therapeutically, we engineered an endothelium targeted, cell membrane hybridized lipid nanoparticle encapsulating Myc siRNA (Lip@siMyc). This system achieved homotypic targeting, vitreal penetration, and sustained Myc gene silencing, and markedly inhibited ocular NV in mice. Notably, Lip@siMyc showed efficacy comparable to aflibercept, and combined treatment produced enhanced anti angiogenic effects. In summary, our findings establish the glycolysis/HBP/Myc axis as a critical regulator of EC proliferation and highlight endothelial Myc blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy for ocular NV.

title: Orchestrating adaptive homeostasis on bioprosthetic valves: a metal-polyphenol hydrogel armor for integrated immunomodulation and endothelialization.
abstract: NA: With the advancement of transcatheter valve replacement technology, bioprosthetic heart valves (BHVs) are being increasingly used in the clinical treatment of valvular diseases. However, current BHVs fail to concurrently resist thrombosis, modulate the immune and redox homeostasis in response to complex host-biomaterial interactions, leading to premature degeneration and shortened lifespan. Herein, we constructed an endothelial layer-inspired armor for BHV by fusing metal-polyphenol drug network (MPN) nanoparticle with immune/redox regulation functions and vascular endothelial glycocalyx-like layer that serve as passive defense and endothelialization scaffolds. The coating established a biomimetic endothelial defense barrier that resisted the deposition of blood components on BHVs while acting as a scaffold for endothelialization. The MPN nanoparticle fabricated through the self-assembly of Epigallocatechin-3-gallate, curcumin, and Cu2+ was anchored to endow the BHV with free-radical-scavenging capability, immunomodulatory activity and endothelialization-promoting potential. The overexpressed reactive oxygen species were scavenged and the local inflammation responses were downregulated through immune and inflammatory response pathways. This not only maintained homeostasis at the BHV bio-interface but also created a pro-endothelialization microenvironment that favors the adhesion and growth of endothelial cells. Additionally, the coating catalyzed the releasing of NO to promote the endothelialization through PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. The combined advantages of nanoparticles and glycocalyx-like hydrogel, which integrate antithrombotic, immunomodulatory, antioxidant, endothelialization-promoting, and anti-calcification effects, provided a promising strategy to address the critical challenge of BHV degeneration.

title: Engineering hypoactivated platelet-derived coating to decouple thrombosis for vascular regeneration.
abstract: NA: The clinical performance of intravascular stents remains limited by thrombotic complications and delayed vascular healing. While cell membrane-based coatings have been explored to recapitulate native biointerfaces, achieving simultaneous hemocompatibility and pro-regenerative functionality remains challenging due to the intrinsic thrombogenicity of platelet-derived materials. Here, we propose a brand-new hypoactivated platelet-derived coating (hPLC) by sequentially assembling fibrin networks and low-activated platelets, followed by controlled lysis to remove pro-thrombotic components. This approach preserves the structural and biointerfacial features of platelet membrane while decoupling thrombogenic activity from regenerative functionality. The resulting hPLC endows materials with reduced protein adsorption, suppressed coagulation, and attenuated inflammatory responses. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals that hPLC enhances endothelial compatibility through coordinated regulation of anti-apoptotic, cytoskeletal remodeling, and angiogenic pathways. In vivo stent implantation studies demonstrate that hPLC-coated stents provide a pro-regenerative microenvironment, significantly accelerating re-endothelialization while inhibiting neointimal hyperplasia and peri-strut inflammation. These findings establish a bioinspired and clinically translatable strategy for engineering multifunctional vascular interfaces from readily available blood components, offering a versatile platform for the surface engineering of vascular devices.

title: Mitochondria-protective polysaccharide augments burn wound repair through immunometabolic reprogramming.
abstract: NA: Effective wound healing requires coordinated extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, immune regulation, and metabolic adaptation-processes governed by fibroblast mitochondria. Conventional burn therapies fail to address the mitochondrial dysfunction that impedes tissue regeneration. Here, we show that colanic acid (CA), a microbial-derived exopolysaccharide, acts as a mitochondrial-protecting biomaterial that accelerates burn repair by restoring immuno-metabolic crosstalk. In a murine deep second-degree burn model, CA enhanced wound closure 3.1-fold over controls, reduced reactive oxidative species by 54%, and increased mature collagen deposition by 193%. Mechanistically, CA undergoes intracellular internalization with the assistance of the membrane receptor TLR4 and maintains mitochondrial integrity, evidenced by restored cristae ultrastructure, a 1.4-fold increase in oxidative phosphorylation flux, and a 1.5-fold elevation in ATP production-effects abolished upon silencing the mitochondrial regulator Thap11. Bulk RNA-seq indicated that CA reshaped the wound immune landscape by driving macrophage recruitment and M2 polarization via mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming. By synchronizing mitochondrial rescue with immune-guided ECM remodeling, CA outperformed hyaluronic acid dressings in wound closure and extracellular matrix remodeling.The preliminary translational proof-of-concept of CA was confirmed in a Bama minipig model of deep second-degree burn wound, where it enhanced re-epithelialization, angiogenesis, and tissue perfusion. Together, these findings suggest that CA is a multifunctional polysaccharide with mitochondrial protective effects capable of addressing the multifaceted pathology of burn wounds across species.

title: Protection against osteoporosis by an osteo-immune niche through FOXP3-dependent systemic immunoregulation.
abstract: NA: Osteo-immune diseases require immunoregulatory strategies that suppress pathological inflammation and restore the balance between immunity and bone remodeling. Here, we demonstrate that a subcutaneously implanted bone-mimetic scaffold generates an ectopic osteo-immune niche that confers systemic protection against osteoporosis. Following implantation, the scaffold elicited a structured foreign body response that organized recruited host cells into a compartmentalized immune microenvironment. And this osteo-immune niche is associated with regulatory immune features, including a FOXP3+ regulatory T cell (Treg)-enriched profile. In an osteoporosis model, this approach was linked to attenuation of systemic bone loss together with immunological changes consistent with an increased Treg population, suggesting that local niche engineering can influence whole-body skeletal health. Collectively, these findings support bone mimetic, immune instructive biomaterial scaffold as a potential therapeutic platform for osteo-immune disorders without the need for complex cell processing.

title: Stress-relaxing and ROS-scavenging hydrogel microspheres restore osteoimmune homeostasis for bone regeneration under mechanoinflammatory conditions.
abstract: NA: Periodontitis drives alveolar bone loss, tooth mobility, and even tooth loss. Although orthodontic treatment can reposition compromised teeth and extend their functional lifespan, orthodontic tooth movement in patients with periodontitis occurs within a mechanoinflammatory microenvironment, where mechanical forces and persistent inflammation synergistically disrupt alveolar bone homeostasis and compromise stem-cell-mediated repair, culminating in bone loss. Breaking this vicious cycle demands a therapy that can simultaneously buffer physical stress and neutralize biochemical insults. Here we report injectable, stress-relaxing, and ROS-scavenging hydrogel microspheres that function as a protective microniche for dental follicle stem cells (DFSCs). Constructed from dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid and phenylboronic acid-modified gelatin, these viscoelastic microspheres rapidly dissipate mechanical stress while their catechol moieties mitigate oxidative damage. Under a combined mechanoinflammatory challenge, the microspheres preserved DFSC viability, stemness, osteogenic potential, and immunomodulatory function. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the microspheres rescued the expression of the DNA repair enzyme OGG1, thereby preventing oxidative DNA damage and suppressing the downstream NF-κB inflammatory cascade. In a murine model of periodontitis-associated orthodontic tooth movement, DFSCs-loaded microspheres not only prevented bone loss but also restored a pro-regenerative osteoimmune homeostasis. Together, this study presents a viscoelastic and redox-active biomaterial-based strategy to safeguard stem cell function and restore osteoimmune balance in mechanically and immunologically challenged tissues.

title: Pathology-adaptive composite hydrogel for efficient suppression of autoimmune uveitis: disrupting bidirectional crosstalk between immune cells and blood-retinal barriers.
abstract: NA: Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a sight-threatening intraocular inflammatory disorder with limited safe therapeutic options. Pathological progression of experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU) follows a temporally staged pattern: early disease onset is driven by aberrant microglial activation that initiates blood-retinal barrier (BRB) disruption, while advanced stages are characterized by reactive oxygen species accumulation and robust infiltration of pathogenic CD44+ immune cells. Capitalizing on this stage-dependent pathological feature, we design a thermosensitive poly (dl-lactide)-b-poly (ethylene glycol)-b-poly (dl-lactide) (PLEL) composite hydrogel (Mino&nanoCur@PLEL) co-loaded with minocycline (Mino) and CD44-targeted curcumin nanoparticles (nanoCur). The engineered platform delivers programmable biphasic drug release to implement stepwise immunomodulation, matching the dynamic EAU pathological process. Rapidly released Mino suppresses early microglial overactivation and stabilizes retinal innate immune homeostasis, whereas sustained nanoCur release enables precise targeting of proinflammatory CD44+ macrophages to block inflammatory cascades and protect BRB structure. In EAU rats, single subconjunctival hydrogel administration efficiently restrains inflammatory deterioration by disrupting the bidirectional proinflammatory interplay between myeloid immune cells and BRB-resident endothelial/retinal pigment epithelial cells, remodeling retinal immune microenvironments and restoring both inner and outer BRB integrity. This pathology-adaptive dual-target immunotherapeutic system offers a translatable precision strategy for AU treatment.

title: Engineering framework-derived carbon enables effective near-infrared photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide generation for cascade cancer therapy.
abstract: NA: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-mediated catalysis is key to oxidative chemical transformations and catalytic cancer therapies. However, its efficiency is limited by the lack of controllable catalytic systems capable of selectively driving two-electron oxygen reduction under physiologically relevant conditions. Herein, photocatalytic H2O2 generation in carbon systems was discovered to be governed by programmable electronic structures rather than material composition. By exploiting a framework-derived transformation, a series of carbon nanostructures were constructed with continuously adjustable electronic states, which enabled correlation between electronic configuration and photocatalytic behavior. Thus, a non-monotonic dependence of activity on graphitization degree was identified, where an intermediate semi-graphitized phase maximizes near-infrared (NIR) absorption, charge separation, and selective two-electron oxygen reduction. In contrast, insufficient conjugation limits excitation efficiency, while excessive delocalization accelerates carrier recombination, defining an electronic-structure window for optimal catalysis. This electronically optimized structure enables NIR-driven H2O2 generation without sacrificial agents, which further couples with Fe2+-mediated Fenton reactions and hole-driven glutathione depletion to achieve a self-amplifying redox cascade for cancer therapy. The as-obtained system achieves efficient oxidative transformation in vitro and significant tumor suppression in vivo. These findings suggest an electronic-structure-associated paradigm for carbon-based photocatalysis and provide a generalizable strategy for modulating reaction selectivity and efficiency in metal-free systems.

title: Pharmacologically programmed tolerogenic dendritic cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for CCR7-dependent lymphoid organ targeting in transplantation.
abstract: NA: Secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) are critical sites for alloimmune activation and attractive targets for transplantation immunotherapy. However, current cell membrane-based targeting strategies face a fundamental trade-off between low immunogenicity and efficient SLO homing, limiting their therapeutic potential. To resolve this functional trade-off, we developed a biomimetic delivery system (PD-DmRK) by coating self-assembled RapaLink-1 (RK) nanoparticles with cell membranes derived from PP242 and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-induced tolerogenic dendritic cells (TolDCs). Compared with conventional tolerogenic induction strategies, PP242/DHA preserved low immunogenicity and markedly increased CCR7 expression, thereby improving SLO targeting. Mechanistically, PP242 and DHA cooperatively activated the transcription factor USF2, which directly bound to the Ccr7 promoter and transcriptionally upregulated Ccr7 expression. Consequently, PD-DmRK exhibited enhanced accumulation in SLOs, reduced hepatic and renal sequestration, and significantly prolonged skin and cardiac allograft survival. High-dimensional spectral flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomic analyses further indicated that PD-DmRK treatment was associated with enrichment of Ccr9-expressing plasmacytoid dendritic cells and regulatory T cells, accompanied by reduced cytotoxic T-cell responses. Overall, PD-DmRK provides a TolDC membrane platform in which the USF2-CCR7 axis links immunoregulatory activity with CCR7-dependent SLO targeting, supporting its potential for targeted immunotherapy in transplantation.

title: Biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip: Real-time visualisation of biomaterial thrombosis at clinical heparin levels.
abstract: NA: Blood-contacting medical device thrombosis causes device failure, embolism and bleeding due to reliance on anti-thrombotic drugs. The interplay between biological, material and flow parameters in medical device thrombosis remains poorly understood. Importantly, tools to evaluate acute, dynamic thrombotic events on materials in real-time are lacking, impacting the successful development and translation of new anti-thrombotic materials. We developed a biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip model to evaluate acute material thrombogenicity in real-time using human whole blood, mimicking clinical heparin doses (0.5-5 U/mL) and shear rates (50-2000 s-1). System validation showed expected platelet adhesion on hydrophilic glass and platelet passivation and detachment at increasing shears on hydrophobic silicone. For the first time, we characterised fibrin events on materials, finding a shear dependent decrease on glass but not silicone, pre-coating materials with albumin abolished fibrin on silicone but not glass, and inhibition of FXIIa reduced but did not abolish fibrin on either material. More and larger fibrin events (aggregation and channel occlusion) occurred at 0.5 U/mL compared to 5 U/mL heparin, and the heparin level did not affect platelet adhesion dynamics. Glass showed the most severe fibrin events, followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC) > silicone > polycarbonate. Most fibrin events occurred in association with platelets and although platelets were P-selectin positive, very few platelets were procoagulant (P-selectin and Annexin V positive). This clinically relevant, biomaterial thrombosis-on-a-chip model could allow biomaterial thrombosis mechanism elucidation and fast-track evaluation and development of anti-thrombotic materials to improve medical device function and reduce adverse thrombotic and bleeding patient outcomes.

title: Transcription activator-like effector base editing delivered by a targeted lipid nanoparticle for therapy of lung cancer.
abstract: NA: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Among them, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all cases, while the mutation of KRAS oncogene plays a crucial role in its formation and metastasis. Here, we report a transcription activator-like effector (TALE) base editor that can accurately identify KRAS gene under the guide of TALE and sgRNA, convert C base to T base, thereby generating a stop codon and blocking the expression of KRAS. Besides, a targeted TALE base editing lipid nanoparticle (targeted TALE LNP) is developed by rationally designing with cancer-targeted EGFR peptide.
